sentences.en: Just a little girl, only 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 只是一个小女孩，年仅十六岁。

sentences.en: Isn't this something miraculous?
sentences.zh: 难道这不是一个奇迹吗？

sentences.en: Wielding her weapons as though they weighed nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 挥舞着她的武器，仿佛它们毫无重量一般。

sentences.en: Indeed, she seems to have been raised for just such a moment, so strong she is and resolute.
sentences.zh: 的确，她似乎正是为了这样的时刻而生，她是如此坚强而坚定。

sentences.en: Her enemies stumble in flight before her.
sentences.zh: 她的敌人仓皇逃窜，在她面前溃不成军。

sentences.en: Not one of them can stand up to her.
sentences.zh: 没有一个人能抵挡她的锋芒。

sentences.en: And all this she does before the gaze of the world.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是在世界的注视下完成的。

sentences.en: She drives her foes out of France.
sentences.zh: 她将敌人驱逐出法国。

sentences.en: She recaptures castles and towns.
sentences.zh: 她收复了一座座城堡和城镇。

sentences.en: Never has anyone seen such formidable deeds.
sentences.zh: 从未有人见过如此惊人的壮举。

sentences.en: Not hundreds, not thousands of men can compare with her.
sentences.zh: 成百上千的人都无法与她相提并论。

sentences.en: Of our brave and able warriors, she is the chief captain.
sentences.zh: 在我们勇敢且有能力的勇士中，她是最高统帅。

sentences.en: Neither Hector nor Achilles can rival her prowess.
sentences.zh: 无论是赫克托还是阿喀琉斯，都无法与她的勇猛匹敌。

sentences.en: But it is God who has wrote this.
sentences.zh: 但这一切是上帝所书写的。

sentences.en: God who leads her on.
sentences.zh: 是上帝在指引着她。

sentences.en: So that's a poem written in July 1429.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一首写于1429年7月的诗。

sentences.en: It would astound people to know that that poem was written by a French woman.
sentences.zh: 人们会惊讶地发现，这首诗竟然是一位法国女性写的。

sentences.en: A French woman.
sentences.zh: 一位法国女性。

sentences.en: One of the most remarkable women, according to Tom Holland, in medieval history.
sentences.zh: 据汤姆·霍兰所说，她是中世纪历史上最杰出的女性之一。

sentences.en: So she's often described as the first professional female writer in Western history.
sentences.zh: 因此，她常被描述为西方历史上第一位职业女作家。

sentences.en: Her name was Christine de Bison.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑。

sentences.en: She was born in Venice, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，她出生在威尼斯。

sentences.en: So maybe I should have given her a little bit of an Italian lilt.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我刚才应该带一点意大利语调来介绍她。

sentences.en: But she came when she was four years old.
sentences.zh: 但她四岁时就来到了这里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she came to France.
sentences.zh: 她来到了法国。

sentences.en: Her father was appointed the court astrologer, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 她的父亲被任命为宫廷占星家，不是吗？

sentences.en: So he was the Anthony Scaramucci, because he's a big fan of astrology.
sentences.zh: 所以他就像是安东尼·斯卡拉穆奇，因为他是占星术的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: She was the Anthony Scaramucci.
sentences.zh: 她就是那个安东尼·斯卡拉穆奇。

sentences.en: The father was the Anthony Scaramucci of medieval history.
sentences.zh: 这位父亲就是中世纪历史上的安东尼·斯卡拉穆奇。

sentences.en: And then in 1389, her husband dropped dead at the plague, Christine.
sentences.zh: 然后在1389年，克里斯蒂娜的丈夫突然死于瘟疫。

sentences.en: She had three small children and a mother and niece to support.
sentences.zh: 她有三个年幼的孩子，还有母亲和侄女要养活。

sentences.en: And she turned to writing poetry.
sentences.zh: 于是她转向了诗歌创作。

sentences.en: And in those days, actually, you could make money by writing poetry.
sentences.zh: 而且在那个年代，事实上，写诗是可以赚钱的。

sentences.en: So good for her.
sentences.zh: 真为她高兴。

sentences.en: She made a fortune.
sentences.zh: 她赚了一大笔钱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She was prolific on a kind of Sandbrookian scale.
sentences.zh: 她的高产达到了桑德布鲁克式的规模。

sentences.en: So in 1405, she boasted that between the years 1399 and the present year, I have compiled 15 major works.
sentences.zh: 所以在1405年，她夸耀说，在1399年到今年之间，我已经编纂了15部主要著作。

sentences.en: Oh, that's good.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太棒了。

sentences.en: But Dominic, that extract from the poem that you just read, that was the last poem she ever wrote.
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，你刚才念的那段诗摘录，那是她写过的最后一首诗。

sentences.en: She wrote it in 1429, and it celebrated a girl who was even more famous, even more remarkable than she was, a girl that Christine called La Pucelle, the maid,
sentences.zh: 她写于1429年，歌颂了一个比她更出名、更杰出的女孩，一个克里斯蒂娜称之为“拉皮塞尔”（La Pucelle，意为圣女/少女）的女孩，

sentences.en: but who is best known today as, of course, Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 但如今人们当然更习惯叫她圣女贞德。

sentences.en: Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 圣女贞德。

sentences.en: So the most famous woman in medieval history, one of the most celebrated women who's ever existed,
sentences.zh: 所以她是中世纪历史上最著名的女性，是有史以来最受赞誉的女性之一，

sentences.en: one of the most famous characters from medieval history of any gender who's existed.
sentences.zh: 也是中世纪历史上无论哪个性别中最著名的标志性人物之一。

sentences.en: So if you think about, you've got a list here of all the people who've written songs about her.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想看，这里有一长串曾为她写过歌的人。

sentences.en: Leonard Cohen, Madonna, Kate Bush, Arcade Fire, Little Mix, The Cranberries.
sentences.zh: 莱昂纳德·科恩、麦当娜、凯特·布什、拱廊之火、混合果汁乐队、小红莓乐队。

sentences.en: You mentioned one of my favorite bands, Orchestral Maneuvers in the Dark.
sentences.zh: 你提到了我最喜欢的乐队之一，黑暗管弦乐团。

sentences.en: They actually wrote two, Joan of Arc and Maid of Orleans.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上写了两首，一首叫《圣女贞德》，一首叫《奥尔良姑娘》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're both excellent.
sentences.zh: 而且两首都很棒。

sentences.en: Yeah, very good.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常好。

sentences.en: And actually, one of them begins, Little Catholic Girl.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中一首的开头就是“天主教小女孩”。

sentences.en: So quite like Christine's poem.
sentences.zh: 所以和克里斯蒂娜的诗很像。

sentences.en: I don't know whether they were influenced by her.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是否受到了她的影响。

sentences.en: Undoubtedly, they were.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他们一定受了影响。

sentences.en: So she's a pop icon, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 所以她是一个流行文化偶像，对吧？

sentences.en: Because she's a teenage girl.
sentences.zh: 因为她是一个十几岁的女孩。

sentences.en: She's a rebel.
sentences.zh: 她是一个反叛者。

sentences.en: She's an outsider.
sentences.zh: 她是一个局外人。

sentences.en: Well, she's doing things that teenage girls shouldn't do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她在做十几岁女孩不该做的事。

sentences.en: And I think that understanding of her, that tradition, it begins with Christine, who is the author of the very first poem ever written about Joan.
sentences.zh: 我认为对她的这种理解和传统，始于克里斯蒂娜，她是历史上第一首关于贞德的诗的作者。

sentences.en: Because, you know, that bit you read, what is Christine celebrating?
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，你读的那段，克里斯蒂娜在庆祝什么？

sentences.en: She's celebrating the fact that, as you've implied, the English are losing and the French are winning.
sentences.zh: 正如你所暗示的，她在庆祝英国人在输，法国人在赢这一事实。

sentences.en: But more than that, she is celebrating the sheer, mad, glorious improbability of what she's describing,
sentences.zh: 但不仅于此，她还在庆祝她所描述的那种纯粹的、疯狂的、光荣的不可思议，

sentences.en: that a little girl only 16 years old is leading an army into battle and what is more winning.
sentences.zh: 一个年仅十六岁的小女孩竟然率领军队投入战斗，而且更了不起的是，她还赢了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the extraordinary thing, I mean, a couple of extraordinary things, she's so young, she's a girl, and she is a peasant girl.
sentences.zh: 是的，最不可思议的是，我是说有几件不可思议的事，她太年轻了，她是个女孩，而且她是个农家女孩。

sentences.en: And to give people a sense who don't know anything about Joan of Arc, we're in the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 为了让对圣女贞德一无所知的人有个概念，我们身处15世纪。

sentences.en: It's the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 那是百年战争时期。

sentences.en: England have had it all their own way.
sentences.zh: 英国人一直顺风顺水。

sentences.en: So far, well, a lot of it their own way.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，嗯，很大程度上都很顺利。

sentences.en: It looks like the English have won the Hundred Years' War, that, you know, we've ended the last series about it with Agincourt and Henry V and his great victories.
sentences.zh: 看起来英国人已经赢得了百年战争，你知道的，我们在上一季的结尾讲到了阿金库尔战役、亨利五世和他的伟大胜利。

sentences.en: And now this is going to be the great turnaround in French history.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这将成为法国历史上巨大的转折点。

sentences.en: And as you say in your notes, Tom, it feels like something less from the pages of history than from the pages of either fantasy, George R.R.
sentences.zh: 正如你在笔记中说的，汤姆，这感觉与其说是历史书上的内容，不如说是来自奇幻小说，比如乔治·R·R·马丁的作品，或者干脆是童话故事。

sentences.en: Martin or something, or indeed a fairy tale.
sentences.zh: 或者干脆是童话故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, because this is a girl who claims that she has been ordered by supernatural voices to save France.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为这是一个女孩，她声称自己奉了超自然声音的命令来拯救法国。

sentences.en: And she puts on male dress, and she rides to the distant court of the king,
sentences.zh: 她穿上男装，骑马前往远在天边的国王宫廷，

sentences.en: and the king amazingly agrees to meet her and is persuaded by her that she has this God-given mission to defeat the king's enemies and to see him crowned.
sentences.zh: 而国王竟然同意接见她，并被她游说相信她肩负着上帝赋予的使命，要击败国王的敌人并见证他加冕。

sentences.en: And she then rides in armour, like a knight, at the head of a great army.
sentences.zh: 随后，她身穿铠甲，像骑士一样率领着庞大的军队骑马出征。

sentences.en: She liberates the famous city of Orléans on the River Loire from a siege.
sentences.zh: 她从卢瓦尔河畔的包围中解放了著名的城市奥尔良。

sentences.en: She then leads the king through enemy territory, and she does indeed succeed in crowning him in a distant cathedral in a city set amid hostile territory.
sentences.zh: 接着，她率领国王穿过敌占区，并且真的成功地在一座位于敌对领土中心的遥远大教堂里为他加冕。

sentences.en: She is then captured, she's put on trial, she's convicted of heresy, and notoriously, she is burnt to death.
sentences.zh: 随后她被俘虏，接受审判，被判异端罪，并如人们所知的那样被火刑处死。

sentences.en: And it is one of, if not the most extraordinary stories in the whole of history.
sentences.zh: 这是整个历史上最非凡的故事之一，即使不是最非凡的。

sentences.en: And I think we're so familiar with it that perhaps you need to kind of do a deep dive to remind yourself of just how astonishing the story is.
sentences.zh: 我想我们对它太熟悉了，以至于你可能需要深入挖掘一番，才能提醒自己这个故事究竟有多么惊人。

sentences.en: And the thing is, that even the greatest of historians have struggled to make sense of her, to make sense of her story.
sentences.zh: 问题是，即使是最伟大的历史学家也一直在努力去理解她，去理解她的故事。

sentences.en: So, have you read The Waning of the Middle Ages?
sentences.zh: 所以，你读过《中世纪的衰落》吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, Johan Huizinger.
sentences.zh: 读过，约翰·赫伊津哈的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a great Dutch historian and published in 1919.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一位伟大的荷兰历史学家，出版于1919年。

sentences.en: And in his study of 15th century Burgundy and northern France, he pointedly omitted Joan, even though she is probably the most famous character from that period.
sentences.zh: 在他对15世纪勃艮第和法国北部的研究中，他刻意省略了贞德，尽管她可能是那个时期最著名的人物。

sentences.en: And this wasn't because he thought that she was unimportant, but absolutely the opposite.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为他认为她不重要，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: So, he wrote about it years later, why he had omitted Joan.
sentences.zh: 因此，他多年后在解释自己为什么省略贞德时写道：

sentences.en: I knew that she would have torn the book I visualized in my mind completely out of balance.
sentences.zh: 我知道她会彻底破坏我脑海中构思的那本书的平衡。

sentences.en: What kept me from introducing her in it was a sense of harmony, that and a vast and reverent humility.
sentences.zh: 阻止我将她引入其中的原因是一种对和谐感的追求，除此之外，还有一种巨大而虔诚的谦逊。

sentences.en: And he said of her that she is a figure more beautiful than any other nation possesses.
sentences.zh: 他评价她说，这是一个比任何其他国家所拥有的都要美丽的女性形象。

sentences.en: And that's a Dutchman.
sentences.zh: 而那是一个荷兰人。

sentences.en: That's a Dutchman.
sentences.zh: 那是一个荷兰人。

sentences.en: But of course, not everybody has agreed with that verdict, have they, Tom?
sentences.zh: 但当然，并不是每个人都同意这个评价，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: Because even at the time, there were a lot of people who, in fact, especially at the time, there were a lot of people who took a very different view of La Pucelle,
sentences.zh: 因为即使在当时，也有很多人，事实上，尤其是在当时，有很多人对拉皮塞尔持有截然不同的看法，

sentences.en: the Maid of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 也就是奥尔良姑娘。

sentences.en: And chief among them were people we've already mentioned, who were, of course, the English.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的，就是我们刚才提到的人，也就是英国人。

sentences.en: So, they absolutely loathed and indeed feared her, didn't they, as not merely a normal mortal enemy, but as a kind of supernatural enemy, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，他们极其厌恶甚至恐惧她，不是吗？不仅把她当作普通的凡人敌人，而是当作某种超自然的敌人，对吧？

sentences.en: Sorceress, a witch.
sentences.zh: 妖术师，女巫。

sentences.en: Yeah, so here is the Duke of Bedford, who was the regent for his infant nephew, Henry VI, during this period.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是贝德福德公爵，在此期间，他是其年幼的侄子亨利六世的摄政王。

sentences.en: And he's summing up The Maid only a week after Christine de Pizan had completed her poem.
sentences.zh: 就在克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑完成她的诗歌仅仅一周后，他就在对这位圣女进行总结。

sentences.en: And his take is very different to Christine's.
sentences.zh: 他的看法与克里斯蒂娜截然不同。

sentences.en: Bedford says of her, she's a loose, infamous, and immoral woman dressed as a man.
sentences.zh: 贝德福德这样评价她：她是一个放荡、声名狼藉、道德败坏、女扮男装的女人。

sentences.en: And he can't leave it alone, because five years later, he's still at it.
sentences.zh: 而且他对此耿耿于怀，因为五年后他依然这么认为。

sentences.en: And he is directly blaming the decline of English fortunes in France on this monstrous sorceress, a disciple and limb of the fiend called the Pucelle,
sentences.zh: 他将英国在法国运势的衰落直接归咎于这个可怕的妖术师，这个被称为圣女的恶魔的信徒和爪牙，

sentences.en: that used false enchantment and sorcery.
sentences.zh: 她使用了虚假的法术和巫术。

sentences.en: And the reason he is simmering, smoldering with rage, is that this, you know,
sentences.zh: 他之所以怒火中烧、愤愤不平，是因为这个，你知道的，

sentences.en: her life and her rise to prominence coincides with the turning point in this long-running struggle between England and France in the 14th and 15th centuries that comes to be called the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 她的一生和崛起恰逢14和15世纪英法长期冲突的转折点，这场冲突后来被称为百年战争。

sentences.en: We've done, you know, a long-running series on it, a couple of seasons, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我们做过，你知道的，关于它的长期系列节目，好几季了，不是吗？

sentences.en: We're now coming to the decisive moment.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正迎来决定性的时刻。

sentences.en: And that's one reason why Christine de Pizan celebrates Joan so much, is that, as Christine puts it, Joan will cast down the English for good, for this is what God wishes.
sentences.zh: 这也是克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑如此大力歌颂贞德的原因之一，正如克里斯蒂娜所说，贞德将彻底打倒英国人，因为这是上帝的意愿。

sentences.en: And this really is a turning point in the history of the sort of intermingled relations between England and France.
sentences.zh: 这确实是英法之间错综复杂的历史关系中的一个转折点。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry to say, I have to warn our listeners, I don't normally agree with trigger warnings, but in this case I do.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，我必须警告我们的听众，我通常不同意触发警告，但在这种情况下我同意。

sentences.en: The English will not come off well in this story.
sentences.zh: 英国人在这个故事里不会有好下场。

sentences.en: So this is basically Theo Heaven.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是西奥的天堂。

sentences.en: It's four episodes of the English behaving both badly and losing.
sentences.zh: 这是四集关于英国人表现糟糕又不断战败的故事。

sentences.en: And Dominic, I'm sure you would join with me in dedicating this series to Theo on that account.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我相信你也会和我一起，为了这个原因将本系列节目献给西奥。

sentences.en: So it's the story of how the English come to lose once and for all the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是英国人如何彻底输掉百年战争的故事。

sentences.en: But I think before that, we should cheer our English listeners up by reprising everything that had gone right for England.
sentences.zh: 但我想在此之前，我们应该通过回顾所有对英国有利的事情来让我们的英国听众振作起来。

sentences.en: So how they had come to invade France, how they come to conquer a lot of it, how they came to seem actually on the verge of winning the war outright.
sentences.zh: 比如他们是如何入侵法国的，他们是如何征服了大部分领土的，他们是如何看起来实际上即将彻底赢得战争的。

sentences.en: Obviously, the English, unlike Joan, unlike Christine, do not think they're the baddies.
sentences.zh: 显然，英国人与贞德不同，与克里斯蒂娜不同，他们不认为自己是坏人。

sentences.en: They think that the French throne rightfully belongs to their king and that a succession of astonishing victories has comprehensively demonstrated the fact that God agrees with this.
sentences.zh: 他们认为法国王位理应属于他们的国王，一系列惊人的胜利已经充分证明了上帝赞同这一点这一事实。

sentences.en: Because otherwise, if the English were not justified invading France, God wouldn't have allowed them to win so many victories over the French.
sentences.zh: 因为否则的话，如果英国人入侵法国是不正义的，上帝就不会允许他们在对法国人的战争中赢得如此多的胜利。

sentences.en: A crucial point here is that England is much smaller and much less populous and much less rich than France.
sentences.zh: 这里的一个关键点是，英国比法国小得多，人口少得多，也远没有法国富有。

sentences.en: So England is the underdog.
sentences.zh: 所以英国是处于劣势的一方。

sentences.en: I think when we started the Hundred Years' War series, we compared it to Ukraine versus Russia.
sentences.zh: 我想当我们开始百年战争系列节目时，我们把它比作乌克兰对俄罗斯。

sentences.en: You know, one giant, one behemoth and a much smaller country that has actually, in this case, launched a preemptive strike,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个庞然大物，一个巨兽，和一个小得多的国家，在这个案例中，实际上发动了一次先发制人的打击，

sentences.en: basically as a defensive measure, and has enjoyed extraordinary success beyond the wildest dreams, you know, you would think, of England's kings.
sentences.zh: 基本上是作为一种防御措施，并且取得了超越英国国王们最大胆梦想的非凡成功。

sentences.en: And England has done very well, and the two kings in particular.
sentences.zh: 英国干得非常出色，尤其是这两位国王。

sentences.en: So one is Edward III, the victor of Cressy and Poitiers, the great kind of roister-doyster of English history.
sentences.zh: 一个是爱德华三世，克雷西和普瓦捷的胜利者，英国历史上伟大的风流人物。

sentences.en: And the other is Henry V.
sentences.zh: 另一个是亨利五世。

sentences.en: So he has won a tremendous victor at the Battle of Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 他在阿金库尔战役中取得了巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: But then he dies.
sentences.zh: 但随后他去世了。

sentences.en: So at the point of his success, at the point at his peak, right, he's become, he's the dominant figure in France, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以在他的成功之巅，在他权力的顶峰，对吧，他成为了法国无可争议的主导人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, he's the leading military figure in the whole of Europe.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是整个欧洲最主要的军事人物。

sentences.en: And if you want to hear the story of Henry V, we did a series on it a year or so ago, and that is episodes 487 and the next three.
sentences.zh: 如果你想听亨利五世的故事，我们大约在一年前做过一个系列节目，那就是第487集以及接下来的三集。

sentences.en: But it's not just the military genius of Henry that had enabled England to impose itself against all the odds on France.
sentences.zh: 但不仅是亨利的军事天才使英国得以克服重重困难将自己强加于法国。

sentences.en: So it also has a very elaborate, centralised framework of government.
sentences.zh: 英国还拥有一个非常精细、高度集中的政府框架。

sentences.en: And this means that under an effective king,
sentences.zh: 这意味着在一位有能力的国王领导下，

sentences.en: the English state is able to kind of raise taxes and recruit troops and provision armies much more effectively than the French king can,
sentences.zh: 英国国家能够比法国国王更有效地征税、招募军队和为军队提供给养，

sentences.en: because in France, the kingdom is kind of divided up into all kinds of different dukedoms and counties and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为在法国，王国被分割成各种不同的公国和伯国等等。

sentences.en: The other advantage that Henry V has in invading France is an incredibly effective military machine.
sentences.zh: 亨利五世在入侵法国时的另一个优势是一部极其高效的军事机器。

sentences.en: And its strength lies in infantry rather than the cavalry that the French tend to prefer.
sentences.zh: 它的力量在于步兵，而不是法国人偏爱的骑兵。

sentences.en: And it's a kind of mix of men-at-arms and longbowmen.
sentences.zh: 这是重装步兵和长弓手的结合。

sentences.en: And longbows traditionally are seen by the English as absolutely what gives them the cutting edge.
sentences.zh: 长弓传统上被英国人视为赋予他们决定性优势的绝对法宝。

sentences.en: So a generation later, Sir John Fortescue, kind of leading analyst of the age, he says, the power of England standeth most upon our poor archers.
sentences.zh: 因此，一代人之后，那个时代的顶尖分析家约翰·福蒂斯丘爵士说：英国的力量主要在于我们贫穷的弓箭手。

sentences.en: And the great demonstration of this was in 1415 at Agincourt, when the French slaughtered as if they were cattle, according to one English chronicle.
sentences.zh: 而这一切最好的证明是在1415年的阿金库尔战役，根据某部英国编年史的记载，当时法军被屠杀得就像牲口一样。

sentences.en: The French high command, the cream of the nobility, decapitated, loads of them perished on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 法国的高层指挥官、贵族中的精华，人头落地，大批人在战场上丧命。

sentences.en: A key figure who we'll be coming back to, an important somebody to remember, the Duke of Alençon.
sentences.zh: 一个我们等会儿会再次提及的关键人物，一个需要记住的重要人物，阿朗松公爵。

sentences.en: So he was the commander of the second of the two French divisions.
sentences.zh: 所以他是法军两个师中第二师的指挥官。

sentences.en: And he had all these holdings in Normandy, which now passed to his six-year-old heir.
sentences.zh: 他在诺曼底拥有所有这些产业，现在这些产业传给了他六岁的继承人。

sentences.en: And they are now very vulnerable, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们现在非常脆弱，不是吗？

sentences.en: So people should remember that.
sentences.zh: 所以人们应该记住这一点。

sentences.en: That six-year-old heir he will be featuring later in this story.
sentences.zh: 那个六岁的继承人将在本故事的后面登场。

sentences.en: And also, as well as the slaughter, there are maybe up to 2,000 French noblemen are captured.
sentences.zh: 而且，除了这场屠杀，可能有多达2000名法国贵族被俘。

sentences.en: And the most distinguished of these is the French king's nephew, the Duke of Orléans, because his title is one of the highest ranking in France.
sentences.zh: 其中身份最高贵的是法国国王的侄子奥尔良公爵，因为他的头衔在法国是级别最高的头衔之一。

sentences.en: He gets taken to England, where he is destined to spend years and years in captivity.
sentences.zh: 他被带到英格兰，注定要在囚禁中度过漫长岁月。

sentences.en: And again, we mention him because the city of Orléans and the Ducal family of Orléans will be playing a key role in Joan's story.
sentences.zh: 同样地，我们提到他，是因为奥尔良城和奥尔良公爵家族将在贞德的故事中扮演关键角色。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Achencourt, tremendous victory.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿金库尔，一场巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: Two years later, Henry V comes back to France and he cuts a swathe through Normandy.
sentences.zh: 两年后，亨利五世重返法国，在诺曼底横扫千军。

sentences.en: One of the places that he systematically absorbs is Alençon, which, as we described, has fallen to this six-year-old heir.
sentences.zh: 他系统性吞并的地方之一就是阿朗松，正如我们所说，它已经落入了这个六岁继承人的手中。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's lost all his inheritance, basically.
sentences.zh: 对，所以他基本上失去了所有的继承权。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: By 1419, Henry has taken Rouen, the chief city of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 到1419年，亨利已经攻占了诺曼底的首府鲁昂。

sentences.en: He now commands the upper River Seine.
sentences.zh: 他现在控制了塞纳河上游。

sentences.en: That means that, basically, Paris is vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，基本上，巴黎变得岌岌可危。

sentences.en: And not only has Henry got the wind in his sails, but the French are in utter chaos and shambles, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 不仅亨利顺风顺水，而且法国也陷入了彻底的混乱和瘫痪，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because, basically, France has descended into anarchy.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上，法国已经陷入了无政府状态。

sentences.en: Yeah, so proficient to commander, though Henry is, there is no way, I think, that he could have been as successful as he turned out to be.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管亨利是一位精干的指挥官，但我认为，如果法国不是乱作一团，没有被一场真正、极其暴力的内战严重撕裂的话，他是绝不可能取得后来那种成功的。

sentences.en: Had France been ordered, had it not been racked, essentially, by a really, really violent civil war.
sentences.zh: 如果法国当时井然有序的话。

sentences.en: And it is so French that the rival factions in the civil war, one of them is named after probably France's greatest wine-growing region, and the other is named after Brandy.
sentences.zh: 而且非常有法国特色的是，内战中的敌对派系，其中一派的名字可能取自法国最伟大的葡萄酒产区，而另一派的名字则取自白兰地。

sentences.en: So it's Burgundy against Armagnac.
sentences.zh: 所以这是勃艮第派对阵阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: And it's Burgundy because the greatest of all the dukes in France is the Duke of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫勃艮第派，是因为法国所有公爵中最伟大的是勃艮第公爵。

sentences.en: And at the time of Henry V's invasion, this is a guy called John the Fearless.
sentences.zh: 在亨利五世入侵时，这个人被称为无畏者约翰。

sentences.en: He has loads of holdings in the east of France, including, obviously, Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 他在法国东部拥有大量产业，显然也包括勃艮第。

sentences.en: So he's a vassal of the French king, but he also has loads of holdings in the low countries.
sentences.zh: 所以他是法国国王的封臣，但在低地国家也拥有大量产业。

sentences.en: And so he's also a vassal of the Holy Roman Emperor.
sentences.zh: 因此他也是神圣罗马帝国皇帝的封臣。

sentences.en: And that means that he kind of has an independence from France that other noblemen in the kingdom tend not to have.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他拥有某种独立于法国的地位，这是王国其他贵族往往不具备的。

sentences.en: And this provokes all kinds of envy and resentment.
sentences.zh: 这激起了各种各样的嫉妒和怨恨。

sentences.en: None of these rival peers individually can compare with the authority of the Duke of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 这些敌对的同僚中，没有任何一个人单打独斗能比得上勃艮第公爵的权威。

sentences.en: But if they all gang up, then they are kind of, you know, they measure up to him.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们联合起来，那么你知道的，他们就能够与他抗衡了。

sentences.en: And the guy who takes the lead in kind of forming them into a posse is a guy called the Count of Armagnac.
sentences.zh: 带头把他们组织成一股势力的人是一个叫阿马尼亚克伯爵的人。

sentences.en: And so this is why you get these two rival factions, the Burgundians and the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么会有这两个敌对派系：勃艮第派和阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: And they start kind of tearing each other to pieces.
sentences.zh: 他们开始互相撕咬。

sentences.en: And to begin with, it looks like the Armagnacs have the upper hand.
sentences.zh: 起初，看起来是阿马尼亚克派占了上风。

sentences.en: And this is because they hold two cards.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们手握两张王牌。

sentences.en: The first, they hold Paris, so the capital of France.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们占领了巴黎，也就是法国的首都。

sentences.en: The Duke of Burgundy and his supporters have been expelled from the capital.
sentences.zh: 勃艮第公爵和他的支持者已被驱逐出首都。

sentences.en: But they also have the backing of the Dauphin, so the heir to the French throne.
sentences.zh: 但他们也得到了王太子（即法国王位继承人）的支持。

sentences.en: He's a guy called Charles.
sentences.zh: 他是一个叫查尔斯的人。

sentences.en: He's 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 他今年16岁。

sentences.en: He's very sickly.
sentences.zh: 他身体非常虚弱。

sentences.en: He's very moody.
sentences.zh: 他喜怒无常。

sentences.en: He has no great self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 他没有什么自信。

sentences.en: He has very spindly legs.
sentences.zh: 他的腿非常纤细。

sentences.en: And essentially, I think even at the age of 16, he has a slight look of Vladimir Putin, only with very rubbery lips.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我认为即使在16岁时，他也有点像弗拉基米尔·普京，只是嘴唇更有弹性。

sentences.en: And the reason that he's been cast in the spotlight is his father has gone completely mad, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他之所以被推到聚光灯下，是因为他的父亲彻底疯了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Charles VI.
sentences.zh: 也就是查理六世。

sentences.en: So then there's a big twist, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 所以接下来有一个巨大的转折，对吧？

sentences.en: An amazing twiSt.
sentences.zh: 一个惊人的转折。

sentences.en: I remember seeing an illustration of this when I was a boy of all of these kind of illustrated book about all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我记得当我还是个男孩的时候，看过一本关于所有这些事情的插图书，里面就有这方面的插图。

sentences.en: And I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: So Burgundian troops in 1419 get into Paris.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1419年，勃艮第军队进入了巴黎。

sentences.en: They batter the Count of Armagnac to death.
sentences.zh: 他们把阿马尼亚克伯爵殴打致死。

sentences.en: They carve his cross, his saltire, from his coat of arms into his flesh.
sentences.zh: 他们把他族徽上的十字和斜交叉纹刻进他的血肉里。

sentences.en: That's a nice detail.
sentences.zh: 真是个绝妙的细节。

sentences.en: There's then a huge pogrom of the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 随后对阿马尼亚克派展开了一场大屠杀。

sentences.en: The Dauphin, the heir to the French throne, basically young Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 王太子，法国王位继承人，基本上就是年轻版的弗拉基米尔·普京。

sentences.en: He has to be smuggled out of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他不得不被秘密偷运出巴黎。

sentences.en: And he sets up a court in Bourges, in central France, which is south of the Loire.
sentences.zh: 他在法国中部卢瓦尔河以南的布尔日建立了一个宫廷。

sentences.en: So that's the context.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时的背景。

sentences.en: While Henry V, from England, he's thinking, yeah, it's all his Christmases, come at once.
sentences.zh: 而来自英格兰的亨利五世则在想，太棒了，简直就像所有的圣诞节一块儿来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's advancing from the north.
sentences.zh: 对，他正从北方推进。

sentences.en: And actually, he gets to the city's gates, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 事实上，他已经兵临城下了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Not long after this, a few months after this, in August 1419.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，几个月后的1419年8月。

sentences.en: And then there's another amazing twist, which is the head of the Burgundians, John the Fearless, and the Dauphin, agree to meet.
sentences.zh: 然后又有一个惊人的转折，那就是勃艮第派首领无畏者约翰与王太子同意会面。

sentences.en: And this is one of my favorite summit meetings in all history.
sentences.zh: 这是我个人在所有历史中最喜爱的首脑会晤之一。

sentences.en: Yes, and it is one of the most notorious episodes and consequential episodes in French history.
sentences.zh: 是的，这也是法国历史上最臭名昭著且最具影响力的事件之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, so this summit is held on the 10th of September on a bridge at Montreux, which is some 50 miles southeast of Paris.
sentences.zh: 是的，这次峰会于9月10日在距离巴黎东南约50英里的蒙特罗的一座桥上举行。

sentences.en: So essentially between Paris and Bourges.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上是在巴黎和布尔日之间。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, it's kind of neutral territory.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道的，这算是一种中立领地。

sentences.en: And the bridge, again, is designed to be a neutral space.
sentences.zh: 而且这座桥的设计也旨在成为一个中立空间。

sentences.en: The problem is it all goes wrong because John the Fearless, the Duke of Burgundy, is assassinated.
sentences.zh: 问题是这一切都搞砸了，因为勃艮第公爵无畏者约翰被暗杀了。

sentences.en: By the Dauphin's men, right?
sentences.zh: 被王太子的人，对吧？

sentences.en: So it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 看来是的。

sentences.en: And certainly, whether the Dauphin personally is responsible for it or not, the son of the Duke of Burgundy, who is now the Duke of Burgundy himself, Philip,
sentences.zh: 当然，无论王太子本人是否应该为此负责，勃艮第公爵的儿子——现在他自己成为了勃艮第公爵——菲利普，

sentences.en: who is known as Philip the Good, he blames the Dauphin for the murder of his father.
sentences.zh: 也就是被称为好人菲利普的人，将他父亲的谋杀归咎于王太子。

sentences.en: And this means that the blood feud between the Burgundians and the Armagnacs is now absolutely entrenched to the degree that Philip the Good, you know,
sentences.zh: 这意味着勃艮第派和阿马尼亚克派之间的血海深仇现在彻底根深蒂固，以至于好人菲利普，你知道的，

sentences.en: his father's body is bleeding.
sentences.zh: 他父亲的尸体还在流血。

sentences.en: Rather than combine with the Dauphin against Henry V and the English, Philip the Good now goes to Henry V and he signs up to an English alliance.
sentences.zh: 好人菲利普没有与王太子联合起来对抗亨利五世和英国人，而是转去找亨利五世，签署了英格利亚同盟。

sentences.en: Crikey, this is a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这可真是个大反转。

sentences.en: So the result of this, basically, is that things are looking terrible for the French because the Burgundians and the English have joined forces.
sentences.zh: 所以这带来的结果基本上就是，法国的形势看起来糟透了，因为勃艮第人和英国人联手了。

sentences.en: And so the following May, basically, the French, they kind of have to yield to the inevitable, don't they?
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的五月，基本上，法国人不得不向不可避免的现实妥协，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, the king does.
sentences.zh: 嗯，国王是这样的。

sentences.en: So Charles VI, who is, by this point, kind of a race-like specter, completely mad.
sentences.zh: 所以查理六世，此时此刻他简直就像一个饱经沧桑的幽灵，彻底疯了。

sentences.en: And so therefore, essentially, a puppet of the Duke of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他基本上成了勃艮第公爵的傀儡。

sentences.en: He is in the city of Troyes in Champagne, which is kind of southeast of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他在香槟省的特鲁瓦城，那是在巴黎东南方向。

sentences.en: Henry V joins Philip and Charles VI there and they draw up a treaty.
sentences.zh: 亨利五世在那里与菲利普和查理六世会合，他们起草了一份条约。

sentences.en: And by the terms of this treaty, Charles VI remains on the French throne until he dies.
sentences.zh: 根据该条约的条款，查理六世将继续在位，直到他去世。

sentences.en: Henry will rule as his regent and he will marry Charles VI's daughter, Catherine.
sentences.zh: 亨利将作为摄政王统治，并迎娶查理六世的女儿凯瑟琳。

sentences.en: On the death of Charles VI, the French crown will pass to Henry and his heirs.
sentences.zh: 查理六世死后，法国王位将传给亨利及其继承人。

sentences.en: So Henry of Lancaster, so to the House of Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 也就是兰开斯特的亨利，即兰开斯特王朝。

sentences.en: And the House of Lancaster will take the place on the French throne of Charles VI's own dynasty, the House of Valois.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特王朝将取代查理六世自己的瓦卢瓦王朝，登上法国王位。

sentences.en: And once England and France have come under the rule of the House of Lancaster, they will be separate kingdoms,
sentences.zh: 一旦英格兰和法国归于兰开斯特王朝的统治之下，它们将成为独立的王国，

sentences.en: but they will be joined under one crown and there will be peace and amity and all will be well.
sentences.zh: 但它们将在同一个王冠下联合起来，将会有和平与友谊，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: And this is the plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的计划。

sentences.en: This is one of the questions we're asked most often at live shows and bonus episodes of the Restless History Club.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在《动荡历史俱乐部》的现场演出和特别节目中最常被问到的问题之一。

sentences.en: What would have happened if Henry V had lived?
sentences.zh: 如果亨利五世活下来了会怎么样？

sentences.en: Would England and France have become one kingdom?
sentences.zh: 英格兰和法国会变成一个王国吗？

sentences.en: And in a way, I think this series answers that question.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，我认为这个系列回答了这个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想确实如此。

sentences.en: But in the meanwhile, obviously for the Dauphin, Charles VI's son, who's now just been disinherited,
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，显然对于王太子——查理六世的儿子，刚刚被剥夺继承权的人来说，

sentences.en: this is terrible news because he's been publicly condemned by his own father as a murderer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的消息，因为他被自己的亲生父亲公开谴责为谋杀犯。

sentences.en: You know, he's been bumped off the line of inheritance and he has no prospect really of defeating Henry V, partly because Henry V is the greatest warrior of the age,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他被踢出了继承序列，而且他几乎没有希望击败亨利五世，部分是因为亨利五世是这个时代最伟大的战士，

sentences.en: but also because the Dauphin can't risk himself in battle.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为王太子不敢亲自冒险上战场。

sentences.en: Because without him, the House of Valois really would be extinct.
sentences.zh: 因为没有了他，瓦卢瓦王朝就真的要绝嗣了。

sentences.en: There is no one else to keep the Valois line going.
sentences.zh: 没有人能继续维持瓦卢瓦家族的血脉。

sentences.en: And then things get even worse because on the 6th of December, 1421, Henry and his new bride, so the sister of the Dauphin, Catherine, Catherine gives Henry V, not just a child,
sentences.zh: 然后情况变得更糟，因为在1421年12月6日，亨利和他的新娘——也就是王太子的妹妹凯瑟琳，凯瑟琳给亨利五世生下的不仅仅是一个孩子，

sentences.en: but a son whom they'd call, with great originality, Henry.
sentences.zh: 而是一个儿子，他们以极具独创性的方式给他取名叫亨利。

sentences.en: The future Henry VI.
sentences.zh: 未来的亨利六世。

sentences.en: And so this means that the House of Lancaster now has an heir.
sentences.zh: 这意味着兰开斯特王朝现在有了一个继承人。

sentences.en: And so a lot of people in France, it's important to, if we stop the clock there, December 1421, France is an anarchy.
sentences.zh: 因此，法国的许多人——如果我们把时钟停在1421年12月这一刻，法国处于无政府状态，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: The English have taken advantage, taken Paris, all of this.
sentences.zh: 英国人占了上风，攻占了巴黎，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Henry is the regent now.
sentences.zh: 亨利现在是摄政王。

sentences.en: He expects to be king.
sentences.zh: 他指望成为国王。

sentences.en: He has a son ready.
sentences.zh: 他已经有了一个现成的儿子。

sentences.en: If you're sitting there in France, you look at this and you say, well, this is how it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 如果你坐在法国，看到这一切，你就会说，好吧，事情就是这样了。

sentences.en: And this is God's plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是上帝的计划。

sentences.en: This is obviously what God wants.
sentences.zh: 这显然是上帝想要的。

sentences.en: And so when people work with Henry, they're not doing so because they're, you know, proto-Marshal Paytans or something.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们与亨利合作时，他们这么做并不是因为他们是什么原始贝当元帅之类的人。

sentences.en: It's not a question of sort of cowardly collaboration.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是懦弱勾结的问题。

sentences.en: It's because they genuinely look at the situation.
sentences.zh: 而是因为他们真正审视了局势。

sentences.en: They say, this is all part of the divine workings out of, you know, of God's intention for the world.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这一切都是上帝对世界的意图的 divine 运作的一部分。

sentences.en: I think also there's a certain grudging respect for Henry V.
sentences.zh: 我也认为人们对亨利五世有一种勉强维持的敬意。

sentences.en: He's a serious person.
sentences.zh: 他是一个严肃的人。

sentences.en: You know, this is a guy who could kind of lick a crumbling kingdom into shape.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这家伙能够把一个濒临崩溃的王国重整旗鼓。

sentences.en: But also, I think for lots of people in France who decide to back the House of Lancaster, it's not really about the English at all.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我认为对于法国许多决定支持兰开斯特王朝的人来说，这根本不是关于英国人的问题。

sentences.en: It's about what your identity is in the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 这关乎你在内战中的身份认同。

sentences.en: So if you back the Armagnacs, you're never going to accept this.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你支持阿马尼亚克派，你永远不会接受这一点。

sentences.en: But if you are a Burgundian sympathizer, then you absolutely are.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是勃艮第派的同情者，那么你绝对会接受。

sentences.en: So in a sense, it's simultaneously the Hundred Years' War and the Civil War between the Burgundians and the Armagnacs have become interfused.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，百年战争与勃艮第派和阿马尼亚克派之间的内战同时交织在了一起。

sentences.en: And this explains why so many people in France are willing to accept the House of Lancaster as a legitimate replacement for the House of Valois.
sentences.zh: 这就解释了为什么法国有那么多人愿意接受兰开斯特王朝作为瓦卢瓦王朝的合法替代者。

sentences.en: And Theo has actually made a good point in the chat, which is that, you know, the English and French ruling classes are so similar, you know,
sentences.zh: 西奥在聊天区里实际上提出了一个很好的观点，那就是，你知道的，英法统治阶层是如此相似，

sentences.en: in their devotion to the ideals of chivalry, in their devotion to kind of the stuff about courtly love, you know, the use of French, all of that stuff,
sentences.zh: 他们对骑士精神理想的奉献，对宫廷爱之类事物的热衷，法语的使用，所有这些，

sentences.en: that it doesn't necessarily feel like you're accepting the rule of kind of foreign barbarians, right?
sentences.zh: 以至于你并不一定会觉得你是在接受外来野蛮人的统治，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm not sure that is entirely true, because this is the first century, really, in which the English aristocracy are not speaking French as their native language.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这是否完全正确，因为这其实是英国贵族不再以法语为母语的第一个世纪。

sentences.en: Ah, interesting.
sentences.zh: 啊，有意思。

sentences.en: So it is noted as something exceptional when an English aristocrat speaks very good French, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我们将会看到的，当一个英国贵族能说一口流利的法语时，这被认为是一件非同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: Here's a quick question then.
sentences.zh: 那么这里有一个快问。

sentences.en: In other words, if this had happened a century or two earlier, the outcome might have been different.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果这件事早发生一个世纪或两个世纪，结果可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: It might indeed, but as it is, there are obviously lots of very distinguished, very clear thinking Frenchmen who are prepared to accept the House of Lancaster and just, you know,
sentences.zh: 确实可能会不同，但事实就是如此，显然有很多非常杰出、头脑清醒的法国人准备接受兰开斯特王朝，并且，你知道的，

sentences.en: plucking at random an example.
sentences.zh: 随手举个例子。

sentences.en: Let's look at one.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看一个。

sentences.en: So he is a very distinguished churchman and he goes by the name of Pierre Cochon.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常杰出的神职人员，名叫皮埃尔·科雄。

sentences.en: He'd been born in Arras, a city to the north of Paris, where by ancient tradition, the kings of France were always crowned.
sentences.zh: 他出生于阿拉斯，这是一座位于巴黎以北的城市，按照古老的传统，法兰西国王总是在那里加冕。

sentences.en: This is where Clovis, the very first king of the Franks to accept Christianity, had been baptised.
sentences.zh: 克洛维，第一位皈依基督教的法兰克国王，就是在这里接受洗礼的。

sentences.en: Cochon had then gone to Paris to study at the university there, which is the greatest centre for theology in the whole of Europe.
sentences.zh: 随后，科雄前往巴黎当地的大学深造，那是整个欧洲最伟大的神学中心。

sentences.en: And there, as a student, he had become a very enthusiastic partisan of the Burgundian cause, hates the Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 在那里求学期间，他成为了勃艮第派狂热的支持者，对阿马尼亚克派恨之入骨。

sentences.en: He's appointed the Bishop of Beauvais, which is a city in Champagne about 50 miles northwest of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他被任命为博韦主教，博韦是香槟地区的一座城市，位于巴黎西北约50英里处。

sentences.en: So his centre of gravity is very much that kind of region, Paris and the region between Paris and the low countries where Burgundy has his centre of gravity.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的势力重心主要就在那个区域，也就是巴黎以及巴黎和低地国家之间勃艮第拥有势力重心的地带。

sentences.en: And Cochon is very, very devoutly convinced that only the Anglo-Burgundian alliance has any prospect of stabilising France.
sentences.zh: 科雄非常、非常笃信地认为，只有英勃联盟才有任何稳定法兰西的前景。

sentences.en: And so he goes full in.
sentences.zh: 所以他全力以赴地加入了进去。

sentences.en: And I think it is unfair to think, you know, you mentioned Marshall Pétain.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，认为……你知道的，你提到了贝当元帅，这种想法是不公允的。

sentences.en: This is not a viciist policy.
sentences.zh: 这并非一种维希式的政策。

sentences.en: I think in the context of the time, it's entirely understandable.
sentences.zh: 我认为在当时的语境下，这是完全可以理解的。

sentences.en: A quick note for listeners.
sentences.zh: 给听众的一个温馨提示。

sentences.en: They should remember this bloke, Pierre Cochon, and his support for this alliance and his role in this story.
sentences.zh: 他们应该记住这家伙，皮埃尔·科雄，以及他对这个联盟的支持和他在这个故事中的角色。

sentences.en: Just keep him in your heads as you listen to this series, because he will play a very, very significant role.
sentences.zh: 在你们收听这个系列节目时，请一直把他记在脑子里，因为他将扮演非常、非常关键的角色。

sentences.en: In the way that if you're reading a detective story and it's mentioned in chapter two, that there's a gun on the mantelpiece,
sentences.zh: 就像如果你在读侦探小说，第二章提到壁炉架上有一把枪一样，

sentences.en: you can be fairly confident that gun is going to go off at some point.
sentences.zh: 你可以相当确信，那把枪在某个时刻一定会开火。

sentences.en: He's going to go off.
sentences.zh: 它迟早会开火。

sentences.en: So Cochon is kind of representative of those who side with the House of Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 所以科雄某种程度上代表了那些站在兰开斯特家族一边的人。

sentences.en: Obviously, there are lots in France who think this is appalling, a disgrace, a humiliation.
sentences.zh: 显然，法兰西有很多人认为这骇人听闻、是个耻辱、是一种羞辱。

sentences.en: And one of them is Christine de Pizan, very loyal to the royal family.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑，她对王室非常忠诚。

sentences.en: You know, she'd been raised in the court and she is so upset by what has happened that this incredibly articulate, prolific poet just falls silent.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她在宫廷中长大，对发生的事情感到如此心烦意乱，以至于这位极具表达力、著作丰盛的诗人陷入了沉默。

sentences.en: And in 1418, she retires to an abbey where her daughter was a nun and she never she doesn't write anything else.
sentences.zh: 1418年，她退隐到了一座修道院，她的女儿在那里当修女，此后她再也没有写过任何东西。

sentences.en: So there are lots of other people who are recording the horrors of the age.
sentences.zh: 因此，还有许多其他人在记录这个时代的恐怖景象。

sentences.en: So, you know, the hunger, the brutality, the wolves padding through the outskirts of Paris, all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如，饥荒、残暴、在巴黎郊外徘徊的野狼，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But Christine is so appalled.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯蒂娜受到了太大的打击。

sentences.en: It's like she's gone into a kind of catatonic shop.
sentences.zh: 这就好比她进入了一种紧张症式的休克状态。

sentences.en: Doesn't doesn't speak at all.
sentences.zh: 一句话也不说。

sentences.en: But then, Tom, there are more twists in this very George R.
sentences.zh: 但随后，汤姆，在这个非常具有乔治·R·R·

sentences.en: R.
sentences.zh: 马丁风格的故事里，

sentences.en: Martin style story.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的波折。

sentences.en: So, first of all, August 1422, Henry V dies unexpectedly young.
sentences.zh: 首先，1422年8月，亨利五世意外地英年早逝。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he never sits on the French throne.
sentences.zh: 所以他从未登上法兰西王位。

sentences.en: And then the guy who is on the French throne, this sort of mad puppet, Charles VI, he dies two months after that.
sentences.zh: 接着，那个坐在法兰西王位上的人，也就是那个近乎疯狂的傀儡查理六世，在那之后两个月也去世了。

sentences.en: So now they're at the equation.
sentences.zh: 所以现在局势变了。

sentences.en: The new king of France, according to the treaty, will be Henry V's infant son, Henry II of France or Henry VI of England.
sentences.zh: 根据条约，新的法兰西国王将是亨利五世的幼子，即法兰西二世或英格兰六世亨利。

sentences.en: But he's a baby.
sentences.zh: 但他还是个婴儿。

sentences.en: So what now for the English?
sentences.zh: 那么英格兰人接下来怎么办？

sentences.en: Well, they're not going to give up on Henry V's dream.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们不会放弃亨利五世的梦想。

sentences.en: And there is a deep personal sense of obligation to Henry V.
sentences.zh: 并且对亨利五世有一种深深的个人责任感。

sentences.en: You know, all the hard men in the English government had fought with him, had been at Agincourt or Normandy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，英格兰政府里所有那些硬汉都曾与他并肩作战，参加过阿金库尔战役或诺曼底战役。

sentences.en: They are absolutely committed to basically to fulfilling this treaty that Henry had done so much to draw up.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对致力于去实现亨利为之付出大量心血拟定的这项条约。

sentences.en: And this is where the Duke of Bedford, who we have already mentioned before, comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们之前已经提到过的贝德福德公爵登场的时候了。

sentences.en: John of Lancaster, the Duke of Bedford.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特的约翰，贝德福德公爵。

sentences.en: He is Henry V's younger brother.
sentences.zh: 他是亨利五世的弟弟。

sentences.en: He is therefore the uncle of Henry VI.
sentences.zh: 因此他是亨利六世的叔叔。

sentences.en: And in France, he is going to serve the infant, Henry VI, as regent.
sentences.zh: 在法兰西，他将作为摄政王辅佐年幼的亨利六世。

sentences.en: So effectively, in France, he is now the head of this kind of Anglo-Burgundian alliance.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，在法兰西，他现在是这种英勃联盟的首脑。

sentences.en: And he is a proper person, right?
sentences.zh: 而且他是个正经人物，对吧？

sentences.en: He's not some...
sentences.zh: 他可不是什么……

sentences.en: I mean, he is...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是……

sentences.en: People may be anticipating because they know the English are going to lose.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会因为知道英格兰人最终会失败而有所预料。

sentences.en: He's a waste of space.
sentences.zh: 觉得他是个废物。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: He is an experienced captain.
sentences.zh: 他是一位经验丰富的统帅。

sentences.en: He's a sensible guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个明理的人。

sentences.en: He's scary.
sentences.zh: 他令人畏惧。

sentences.en: He ticks every box.
sentences.zh: 他各项条件都很完美。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a churchman in Rouen, which, along with Paris, is one of the kind of the two major centers of English power in France.
sentences.zh: 因此，鲁昂的一位神职人员说——鲁昂与巴黎一样，是英格兰在法兰西的两大主要权力中心之一——

sentences.en: And this churchman says of Bedford, wise and generous, at once feared and loved.
sentences.zh: 这位神职人员这样评价贝德福德：明智而慷慨，既令人畏惧又受人爱戴。

sentences.en: And there's a brilliant observation by Jonathan Sumption in the last of his enormous volumes on the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·萨姆森在他关于百年战争的数卷巨著的最后一卷中，有一个精彩的观察。

sentences.en: And he says that Bedford maintained a standing army in France, to quote Sumption, something which England would not have a gain until the time of Oliver Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 他说贝德福德在法兰西维持了一支常备军，用萨姆森的话说，“这是英格兰自奥利弗·克伦威尔时代以来就再也没有过的”。

sentences.en: And there is something slightly of Cromwell, I think, about Bedford.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，贝德福德身上确实有点克伦威尔的影子。

sentences.en: He's very robuSt.
sentences.zh: 他非常强健。

sentences.en: He's also a very civilized man.
sentences.zh: 他也是一个非常文明的人。

sentences.en: So it's noted that he speaks good French.
sentences.zh: 人们注意到他法语说得很好。

sentences.en: He's a great patron of French churches, of French artists.
sentences.zh: 他是法兰西教堂和法兰西艺术家的伟大赞助人。

sentences.en: He's married to the sister of Philip the Good, Anne.
sentences.zh: 他娶了善良的菲利普的妹妹安妮。

sentences.en: So he has a French wife.
sentences.zh: 所以他有一个法兰西妻子。

sentences.en: So he is absolutely able to keep the French administration on side, because even though most of the military are English, the civilian government is French.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他完全能够让法兰西的行政官员站在自己一边，因为尽管大部分军队是英格兰人，但文官政府是法兰西的。

sentences.en: And the fact that Bedford is so impressive, this is why people like Cauchon are so happy to serve him.
sentences.zh: 由于贝德福德如此令人印象深刻，这就是为什么像科雄这样的人会如此乐意为他效劳。

sentences.en: It's the best rule of France ever had, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是法兰西有史以来最好的统治，汤姆。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, what if the Dauphin, or in fact, Charles VII, as he now properly is, if you're backing the House of Valois.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，王太子又如何呢，或者说，如果你支持瓦卢瓦家族的话，他现在实际上已经是查理七世了。

sentences.en: But the thing is, nobody is calling him Charles VII.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，没有人叫他查理七世。

sentences.en: They're all still calling him the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 大家仍然都叫他王太子。

sentences.en: Because he seems an insubstantial figure still.
sentences.zh: 因为他看起来依然是一个无足轻重的人物。

sentences.en: And so I think the Dauphin, recognising this, has been doing his best to try and balance that out.
sentences.zh: 所以我想王太子意识到了这一点，一直在尽最大努力来平衡这种局面。

sentences.en: So he's got himself a queen.
sentences.zh: 于是他给自己找了个王后。

sentences.en: So he has married a girl called Marie.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一个名叫玛丽的女孩。

sentences.en: And she is the daughter of a very, very impressive woman.
sentences.zh: 她是一个非常、非常了不起的女性的女儿。

sentences.en: She's called Yolande.
sentences.zh: 她叫约兰德。

sentences.en: And she is the Dowager Duchess of Anjou.
sentences.zh: 她是安茹的太妃。

sentences.en: So the Angevins, I mean, they're a very serious dynasty.
sentences.zh: 所以安茹家族，我的意思是，这是一个非常显赫的王朝。

sentences.en: And she's probably the most formidable woman in the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 她可能是王国中最令人生畏的女性。

sentences.en: So she's described by one fan as the wisest and most beautiful princess in Christendom.
sentences.zh: 因此她被某位崇拜者描述为“基督教世界中最明智、最美丽的公主”。

sentences.en: She's seen all the other princesses.
sentences.zh: 她可是见过所有其他公主的。
