sentences.en: But that said, we know about Joan.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，我们确实了解贞德。

sentences.en: And we can hear her in her own words in a way that is incredibly unusual for people from the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 而且我们能听到她用自己的原话表达，这对于中世纪的人来说是极其罕见的。

sentences.en: Well, especially young women from peasant background, you never hear from them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尤其是出身农民阶层的年轻女性，你从来听不到她们的声音。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because that is what's really extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 因为这才是真正非同寻常的地方。

sentences.en: You know, we're not hearing a duke or an abbot or a king talking.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们听到的不是某个公爵、修道院长或国王在说话。

sentences.en: We are hearing a young peasant girl.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的是一个年轻的农家女孩。

sentences.en: And when you read the records of the trial, her personality completely shines through.
sentences.zh: 当你阅读审判记录时，她的个性完全闪耀出来。

sentences.en: I'm going to lay my cards on the table.
sentences.zh: 我要摊牌了。

sentences.en: Dominic, you may disagree.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你可能会不同意。

sentences.en: But she is witty.
sentences.zh: 但她机智过人。

sentences.en: She is courageous.
sentences.zh: 她勇敢无畏。

sentences.en: She's incredibly charismatic.
sentences.zh: 她极具个人魅力。

sentences.en: And it's these records, I think, that have really burnished her story in the modern period.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这些记录，真正擦亮了她在现代时期的传奇色彩。

sentences.en: She's up there with Emma Hamilton and Unity in your pantheon.
sentences.zh: 在你的名人堂里，她和艾玛·汉密尔顿以及尤妮蒂齐名。

sentences.en: So she's not an aristocrat like Unity Mitford.
sentences.zh: 所以她不像尤妮蒂·米特福德那样是个贵族。

sentences.en: She, you know, she's not a courtesan like Emma Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 她，你知道的，不像艾玛·汉密尔顿那样是个交际花。

sentences.en: And she's kind of unique.
sentences.zh: 她可以说是独一无二的。

sentences.en: So there's a brilliant book that I read when I was at a very impressionable age by Marina Warner.
sentences.zh: 所以在我极易受影响的年纪，我读过玛丽娜·华纳写的一本精彩的书。

sentences.en: I think it came out in the early 80s called Joan of Arc, The Image of Female Heroism.
sentences.zh: 我想那是80年代初出版的，叫作《圣女贞德：女性英雄主义的形象》。

sentences.en: And in her introduction, Marina Warner says of Joan that, you know, she's not a queen.
sentences.zh: 玛丽娜·华纳在序言中谈到贞德时说，她不是女王。

sentences.en: She's not a courtesan.
sentences.zh: 她不是交际花。

sentences.en: She's not a beauty, not a mother, not an artist of one kind or another, nor until the extremely recent date of 1920 when she was canonized a saint.
sentences.zh: 她不是美人，不是母亲，不是某种意义上的艺术家，而且直到1920年她被册封为圣徒这个极其晚近的日期之前。

sentences.en: To reiterate, she is a female teenage peasant girl.
sentences.zh: 重申一遍，她只是一个十几岁的农村女 peasant（女孩）。

sentences.en: And when we hear her speak,
sentences.zh: 当我们听到她说话时，

sentences.en: I think what we're also hearing all the more loudly is the silence of all those kind of numberless peasants from medieval Christendom whose words no one ever thought to record.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们同时听到的更加响亮的声音，是中世纪基督教世界里那些无数底层农民的沉默，他们的言论从未有人想过去记录。

sentences.en: So this is very moving from you.
sentences.zh: 你这番话真让人感动。

sentences.en: I do find it a moving story.
sentences.zh: 我确实觉得这是一个感人的故事。

sentences.en: I find it a powerful story.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个极具力量的故事。

sentences.en: And I find the fact that we can hear her words, it is a crucial part of what makes this story so fascinating, I think.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我们能听到她的原话这一事实，正是让这个故事如此迷人的关键部分。

sentences.en: So let me just pledge to the listeners that I will suspend my natural skepticism and cynicism for at least the next 30 seconds.
sentences.zh: 所以我向听众保证，我将收起我天生的怀疑和冷嘲热讽，至少在接下来的30秒内如此。

sentences.en: Let's talk about her family.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈她的家庭吧。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you are going to have lots to be skeptical about.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，你会有很多值得怀疑的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, there is no question about that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: Okay, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢。

sentences.en: So let's talk about what we know.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈我们所知道的。

sentences.en: Let us start with her family.
sentences.zh: 让我们从她的家庭开始。

sentences.en: So we know that her father was called Jacques d'Arc, Jacques of Arc.
sentences.zh: 我们知道她的父亲叫雅克·达克（Jacques d'Arc）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so that's where the name Jeanne d'Arc comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是名字让娜·达克（Jeanne d'Arc）的由来。

sentences.en: Her mother is Isabel.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲是伊莎贝尔。

sentences.en: We know that her mother must have been pious because Joan says, from my mother, I learned my Lord's Prayer, my Hail Mary and my Creed.
sentences.zh: 我们知道她的母亲一定很虔诚，因为贞德说：从我母亲那里，我学会了主祷文、圣母经和信经。

sentences.en: And we know that she had a sister and three brothers, two of whom will feature in this story.
sentences.zh: 我们还知道她有一个姐姐和三个兄弟，其中有两个将在这段故事中出场。

sentences.en: And we've described them as peasants, but they're not the underclass.
sentences.zh: 我们把他们描述为农民，但他们不是社会底层。

sentences.en: They're not the lowest of the low, are they?
sentences.zh: 他们不是最底层的人，对吧？

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: And she's actually, it's often said she's a shepherd girl.
sentences.zh: 而且人们经常说她是个放羊的女孩。

sentences.en: I mean, that's one of the most common things that people say about her.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是人们关于她最常说的言论之一。

sentences.en: But she wasn't.
sentences.zh: 但她并不是。

sentences.en: They were more respectable than that, right?
sentences.zh: 他们的地位比那更体面，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不对。

sentences.en: And I think the idea that she's a shepherd, there are kind of biblical echoes there.
sentences.zh: 我认为认为她是牧羊女的说法带有某种圣经色彩。

sentences.en: That's why it suited people who were praising her to say it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么赞美她的人喜欢这么说。

sentences.en: But Joan herself was having none of it.
sentences.zh: 但贞德本人可不买账。

sentences.en: She regarded shepherdesses with a great deal of snobbery.
sentences.zh: 她对牧羊女抱有相当大程度的势利心态。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不会吧。

sentences.en: She's Virginia Woolf.
sentences.zh: 她简直是弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫。

sentences.en: So in her trial, she said, I learned to spin and to sew.
sentences.zh: 所以在审判中她说，我学会了纺纱和缝纫。

sentences.en: And she challenged the women of Rouen to spin and sew better than her.
sentences.zh: 她还向鲁昂的妇女发起挑战，要比她纺纱和缝纫得更好。

sentences.en: And she does this because to be a seamstress, to be a spinner, a spinster, is, you know, you're on a higher level than a shepherdess.
sentences.zh: 她这样做是因为作为一个女裁缝、一个纺纱工，你知道的，你的阶层要比牧羊女高出一个级别。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So she's from Domremy.
sentences.zh: 所以她来自栋雷米。

sentences.en: And the location of this place is interesting and really important because it is, dare I say, liminal.
sentences.zh: 这个地方的地理位置很有趣，也极其重要，因为恕我直言，它具有某种“边缘性”。

sentences.en: It's on the frontier between two different places, Champagne and Lorraine.
sentences.zh: 它位于两个不同地区——香槟和洛林——的交界处。

sentences.en: The river Meuse runs through it.
sentences.zh: 默兹河穿村而过。

sentences.en: And the fact that it's on a frontier is important because it's basically drawn into the civil war by definition.
sentences.zh: 它处于边境这一事实非常重要，因为这意味着它注定会被卷入内战。

sentences.en: Because the village is pro-Dauphin, but the next village is pro-Burgundian.
sentences.zh: 因为这个村庄支持王太子，而隔壁村庄则支持勃艮第派。

sentences.en: And the villagers fight each other quite often, don't they?
sentences.zh: 村民们经常大打出手，不是吗？

sentences.en: And people are badly wounded or even killed in the fighting between these two villages.
sentences.zh: 在这两个村庄的冲突中，有人身受重伤甚至丧命。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And also Domremy is on the front line of the English attempt to annex the region and pacify it completely.
sentences.zh: 而且，栋雷米正处于英国人试图吞并该地区并彻底平定它的最前线。

sentences.en: So as Joan is growing up, there are more and more English raiding parties who are starting to see them on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着贞德的长大，越来越多的英国袭击小分队开始在地平线上出现。

sentences.en: And they are fighting with rival companies who are loyal to the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 他们与效忠于王太子的敌对武装团伙交战。

sentences.en: And this notion of free companies, something we've talked about throughout our series on the Hundred Years' War, these are kind of semi-freelance bodies of men,
sentences.zh: 这种“自由佣兵团”的概念——我们在整个百年战争系列节目中都探讨过——是一群半自由职业的武装人员，

sentences.en: lots of whom are pretty criminal.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人劣迹斑斑、形同罪犯。

sentences.en: And so it's very, very frightening.
sentences.zh: 所以情况非常非常可怕。

sentences.en: It's kind of a Wild West situation.
sentences.zh: 这有点像美国西部的蛮荒局势。

sentences.en: The bad guys galloping into town.
sentences.zh: 恶棍们策马冲进镇里。

sentences.en: And we know that this does happen to Domremy and to other villages around.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，栋雷米以及周边的其他村庄确实遭遇过这种情况。

sentences.en: So when Joan was 11, her cousin was killed by a cannonball that was fired into the church of a neighbouring village where he'd taken refuge.
sentences.zh: 因此，在贞德11岁时，她的表弟被一颗炮弹炸死，那枚炮弹射入了邻村的一座教堂，当时他正避难于此。

sentences.en: And then the church in Domremy itself is burnt down and most of the village with it at least once.
sentences.zh: 随后，栋雷米本地的教堂以及村里的大部分建筑至少被烧毁过一次。

sentences.en: And so for Joan, the ringing of church bells, which are sounded when danger is threatening, you know, this would have been something with which she was very, very familiar.
sentences.zh: 对贞德来说，当危险逼近时敲响的教堂钟声，你可以想象，这是她再熟悉不过的声音了。

sentences.en: So in the summer of 1428, so this is the same year that the English are landing to head down for the siege of Orléans,
sentences.zh: 因此，在1428年夏天——也就是英国人登陆并准备南下围攻奥尔良的同年，

sentences.en: an Anglo-Burgundian army embarks on the systematic conquest of the region.
sentences.zh: 一支英勃联军开始了对该地区的系统性征服。

sentences.en: All the Dauphinist strongholds fall, all except one.
sentences.zh: 所有效忠王太子的据点纷纷陷落，无一幸免，只有一个除外。

sentences.en: And this is a fortress called Vaucouleur, which is very formidable, has a large garrison,
sentences.zh: 这是一座名为沃库勒尔的要塞，防守极为坚固，驻军众多，

sentences.en: and it's under the command of a nobleman from Lorraine by the name of Robert de Baudricourt.
sentences.zh: 由一名名叫罗贝尔·德·博德里库尔的洛林贵族统领。

sentences.en: And de Baudricourt has very good connections at the French court and specifically with the house of Anjou.
sentences.zh: 德·博德里库尔在法国宫廷，特别是与安茹家族有着极好的关系。

sentences.en: So that is Yolande and her dynasty.
sentences.zh: 也就是约兰德和她的王朝。

sentences.en: And de Baudricourt is very brave, but he's also brutal and unscrupulous.
sentences.zh: 德·博德里库尔非常勇敢，但也冷酷无情、不择手段。

sentences.en: And you have to assume that basically you have to be brutal and unscrupulous if you're going to hold a fortress against the onslaught of the English and the Burgundians.
sentences.zh: 你可以想见，面对英国人和勃艮第人的疯狂猛攻，要想守住一座要塞，你基本上就得冷酷无情、不择手段。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So that's the background.
sentences.zh: 这就是背景。

sentences.en: So Joan has been growing up in Domremy in this very violent, frightening, dangerous, divided landscape.
sentences.zh: 因此，贞德是在栋雷米这样一个充满暴力、恐惧、危险和分裂的环境中长大的。

sentences.en: And how does that shape her character, would you say?
sentences.zh: 依你之见，这会对她的性格产生怎样的影响？

sentences.en: Well, I think that it leads her to identify the Dauphin as the kind of the ultimate guarantor of France's stability.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这促使她将王太子视为法国稳定终极的担保人。

sentences.en: I think she comes to have a sense that if only the Dauphin could be put on his throne and crowned and the English could be driven out, then everything would be fine.
sentences.zh: 我认为她逐渐产生了一种信念：只要能让王太子登基加冕，把英国人赶走，一切就都会好起来。

sentences.en: And Marina Warner is brilliant on this in her book, Talking of Joan.
sentences.zh: 玛丽娜·华纳在她关于贞德的书《谈论贞德》中对这一点有着精彩的论述。

sentences.en: She had a natural inclination for clear-cut situations with identifiable centers of authority.
sentences.zh: 她天生倾向于局势明朗、有着明确权力中心的情境。

sentences.en: The king's supreme position and her magnetic attraction for it bear witness to this taste.
sentences.zh: 国王至高无上的地位以及她对这种地位的强烈向往，正是这种性格偏好的证明。

sentences.en: She'd like to unity, organization, rallied groups.
sentences.zh: 她向往统一、秩序和凝聚起来的群体。

sentences.en: So she's basically a kind of working-class Tory.
sentences.zh: 所以她基本上可以说是某种“工人阶级保守派”。

sentences.en: That's, you know, that's what she wants.
sentences.zh: 这就是，你知道的，这就是她所追求的。

sentences.en: She wants order and she wants royal rule.
sentences.zh: 她渴望秩序，渴望王权统治。

sentences.en: But she's also intensely pious.
sentences.zh: 但她同时也极其虔诚。

sentences.en: And again, you can see why, you know, you're growing up surrounded by this violence and the sounding of the bells is what alerts you to danger coming.
sentences.zh: 同样，你也能理解原因：你在这种暴力环境中长大，钟声的敲响就是提醒你危险降临的信号。

sentences.en: So I guess just subliminally, you would come to associate bells with the hope of safety, with the prospect that warnings may be coming.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，潜移默化地，你就会把钟声与对安全的期盼、与警告即将到来的征兆联系在一起。

sentences.en: And so bells seem to have been very, very important to her, to have played a very, very strong role in her emotional and spiritual life.
sentences.zh: 因此，钟声对她而言似乎非常非常重要，在她的大脑和精神生活中扮演着极其强烈的角色。

sentences.en: And so we know from the court records that because a friend of hers recorded it, you know, at her rehabilitation trial,
sentences.zh: 从法庭记录中我们得知——因为她的一个朋友在翻案审判中作证提及，

sentences.en: that once the sacristan forgot to ring the bells for Compline and Joan told him off and said, go and ring them.
sentences.zh: 有一次，司祭长忘记在晚祷时敲钟，贞德还斥责了他，让他快去敲钟。

sentences.en: And if she was out in the fields and she heard the bells ringing, she would always kneel.
sentences.zh: 如果她在田野里听到钟声响起，她总是会跪下来。

sentences.en: They have an immense significance for her.
sentences.zh: 钟声对她具有极其重大的意义。

sentences.en: And I think that you said she's pious.
sentences.zh: 我想你刚才说她很虔诚。

sentences.en: I mean, she clearly is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她显然如此。

sentences.en: But I think what the bells, when she hears the bells, she is being reminded and reassured that amid all the violence of the age,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，当她听到钟声时，钟声在提醒她、安慰她：在那个时代的种种暴力之中，

sentences.en: there is a link to God and his saints and that they are close to her.
sentences.zh: 她与上帝及其圣徒之间依然存在着联系，他们离她很近，

sentences.en: They care for her and that her prayers will be heard.
sentences.zh: 他们关爱着她，她的祈祷会被倾听。

sentences.en: And she can't read and write.
sentences.zh: 她不识字。

sentences.en: She's illiterate.
sentences.zh: 她是个文盲。

sentences.en: But you mentioned God and his saints.
sentences.zh: 但你提到了上帝和他的圣徒。

sentences.en: She's pretty obsessed with some of these saints, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 她对其中一些圣徒相当着迷，不是吗？

sentences.en: And she regards them.
sentences.zh: 并且她尊崇他们。

sentences.en: I mean, we did an episode a long time ago about Catherine of Siena, about somebody, another teenage girl whose proximity, you know, who had this almost obsessive,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很久以前我们做过一期关于锡耶纳的凯瑟琳的节目，那是关于另一个十几岁的女孩，她与……有着这种几乎可以说是痴迷的、

sentences.en: this totally transcendent and dominating fixation with, you know, being the bride of Christ and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 近乎超凡脱俗且占据统治地位的执念，比如渴望成为基督的新娘诸如此类的事。

sentences.en: And there's sometimes I think about Joan, there's something similar.
sentences.zh: 有时我想起贞德，觉得有异曲同工之妙。

sentences.en: Again, a teenage girl, a sort of fixation on this case, on the personalities of three saints in particular.
sentences.zh: 同样是一个十几岁的少女，对特定三位圣徒的个性产生了一种执念。

sentences.en: There are certainly similarities, and we'll maybe come to them later in the series with Catherine of Siena.
sentences.zh: 这确实有相似之处，我们在本系列后面的节目中也许会谈到她与锡耶纳的凯瑟琳的对比。

sentences.en: But I think there are also differences.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为它们存在差异。

sentences.en: And the key one is that Joan, unlike Catherine, as we've said, is illiterate.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，正如我们所说，贞德不像凯瑟琳，她是个文盲。

sentences.en: And therefore, she is dependent on both stories and images.
sentences.zh: 因此，她只能依赖各种故事和图像。

sentences.en: And we know she loves stories.
sentences.zh: 我们知道她喜欢听故事。

sentences.en: She loves chivalric romances, for instance.
sentences.zh: 比如，她喜欢骑士传奇。

sentences.en: She's very familiar with these.
sentences.zh: 她对这些非常熟悉。

sentences.en: But she also loves stories of the saints.
sentences.zh: 但她也喜欢圣徒的故事。

sentences.en: And I don't think she's unusual in her familiarity with them.
sentences.zh: 我认为她对这些故事的熟悉程度并不算稀奇。

sentences.en: The leading saints, the most famous saints, are as familiar to children growing up in medieval Europe this time as kind of singers or sports stars would be to teenagers today.
sentences.zh: 当时的欧洲中世纪，对于在当地长大的孩子们来说，那些主要的、最著名的圣徒就像今天青少年眼中的歌手或体育明星一样耳熟能详。

sentences.en: But there are three, it seems, who are the particular focus of her devotion.
sentences.zh: 但其中似乎有三位是她倾注特别崇敬的核心。

sentences.en: And the first of these is really unsurprising.
sentences.zh: 这其中的第一位其实并不让人意外。

sentences.en: It's St. Michael, who is the great warrior archangel, the captain of heaven, who, in the book of Revelation, throws down Satan.
sentences.zh: 那就是圣米迦勒，伟大的武士大天使、天国军队的统帅，他在《启示录》中将撒旦击落。

sentences.en: And for the French, he is the great emblem of their resistance.
sentences.zh: 对于法国人来说，他是他们顽强抵抗的伟大象征。

sentences.en: So we've said how Henry V conquered all of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 我们之前说过亨利五世征服了整个诺曼底。

sentences.en: That's not quite true.
sentences.zh: 其实这并不完全准确。

sentences.en: Because playing the role of Asterix's village in this scenario is Mont Saint-Michel, the mount of St. Michael, the great monastery there on this island.
sentences.zh: 因为在这个剧本里扮演高卢村庄（注：指《阿斯特里克斯历险记》中抵抗罗马的村庄）角色的，正是圣米迦勒山——那座岛上伟大的圣米迦勒修道院。

sentences.en: And that is holding out against the English.
sentences.zh: 它一直在抵抗英国人。

sentences.en: And so the fact that it is dedicated to St. Michael, it emphasizes the way in which this warrior archangel is presumed by the French to be fighting on their side.
sentences.zh: 因此，这座岛屿献给圣米迦勒这一事实，强调了法国人所设想的这位武士大天使正在站在他们这一边战斗。

sentences.en: And so the Dauphin commissions two great standards, both of which show St. Michael trampling down the serpent, trampling down Satan.
sentences.zh: 于是，王太子委托制作了两面巨幅军旗，上面都描绘了圣米迦勒践踏恶龙、践踏撒旦的图案。

sentences.en: And more specifically, and one of the reasons why Joan is definitely familiar with him, he's the patron saint of the region in which she is growing up.
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，也是贞德必定熟悉他的原因之一，他是她长大的那个地区的守护圣徒。

sentences.en: So St. Michael, very significant.
sentences.zh: 所以圣米迦勒意义重大。

sentences.en: So you can see that.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以理解这一点。

sentences.en: And then there's two female saints.
sentences.zh: 接下来是两位女性圣徒。

sentences.en: And you can see why they would appeal to a teenage girl who perhaps, well, these are saints who are noted for their resistance, for their courage.
sentences.zh: 你能理解为什么她们会吸引一个十几岁的女孩——或许，这些圣徒以坚贞不屈和勇敢闻名。

sentences.en: Also, I found being harsh a little bit for their victimhood or their martyrdom, right?
sentences.zh: 另外，我发现人们也多少会被她们的牺牲或殉道所触动，对吧？

sentences.en: They're martyred rather than surrender their virginity.
sentences.zh: 她们宁死不从、誓死保全贞洁而殉道。

sentences.en: So I guess to Joan, they are emblems of courage and independence.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，对贞德来说，她们是勇气和独立的象征。

sentences.en: And one of them, St. Catherine of Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是亚历山大的圣凯瑟琳。

sentences.en: Again, it's not just Joan who's devoted to her.
sentences.zh: 同样，不仅是贞德对她无比虔诚。

sentences.en: She's probably the best loved saint of the age.
sentences.zh: 她可能是那个时代最受爱戴的圣徒。

sentences.en: And actually, Joan's sister, who died while she was still a girl, had been called Catherine.
sentences.zh: 事实上，贞德在童年夭折的姐姐就叫凯瑟琳。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so Catherine of Alexandria, she was meant to be married to a pagan Roman emperor or something.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大凯瑟琳的故事是，她本应嫁给一个异教的罗马皇帝之类的人。

sentences.en: She's broken on a wheel, hence the Catherine wheel, the firework.
sentences.zh: 她被绑在车轮上受刑，因此有了“凯瑟琳轮”（一种烟花的名字）的说法。

sentences.en: And everyone thinks she's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 每个人都觉得她了不起。

sentences.en: And then the other one is, I have to admit, I'm not familiar with her work.
sentences.zh: 然后另一位是——我必须承认，我对她的事迹不太熟悉。

sentences.en: And that is Margaret of Antioch.
sentences.zh: 那就是安条克的玛格丽特。

sentences.en: Well, I'm very familiar with her because she was swallowed by a dragon and then regurgitated.
sentences.zh: 哦，我对她非常熟悉，因为她曾被一条巨龙吞进肚子里，然后又被吐了出来。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: She's become the patron saint of midwives.
sentences.zh: 她后来成了助产士的守护圣徒。

sentences.en: And Sadie, my wife, of course, is a midwife.
sentences.zh: 而我的妻子萨迪，当然就是一名助产士。

sentences.en: So very big news here.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一条重磅新闻。

sentences.en: But she's another saint who was martyred for refusing to surrender her virginity.
sentences.zh: 但她也是另一位为了拒绝出卖贞洁而殉道的圣徒。

sentences.en: So that's clearly something that Joan is alert to.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然是贞德所关注的一点。

sentences.en: But also, there is a story of St. Margaret.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一个关于圣玛格丽特的故事。

sentences.en: She's so desperate to learn the scriptures and so on that she enters a monastery disguised as a man.
sentences.zh: 她极度渴望学习经文等等，以至于她女扮男装混入了一座修道院。

sentences.en: Oh, a telling detail.
sentences.zh: 哦，一个意味深长的细节。

sentences.en: Very telling detail.
sentences.zh: 非常意味深长的细节。

sentences.en: So just on this thing about the saints, I think this is massively important for listeners who are not super familiar with the world of medieval Christendom to get into their heads.
sentences.zh: 所以，就圣徒这个话题而言，我认为对于那些对中世纪基督教世界不太熟悉的听众来说，让他们脑海中建立这个概念至关重要。

sentences.en: The point of the saints for somebody like Joan, who is, as you said, illiterate, is that they occupy a space between the concrete, physical,
sentences.zh: 对于像贞德这样——正如你所说——目不识丁的人来说，圣徒的意义在于，他们占据了一个空间：

sentences.en: very violent and brutal and dangerous world of 15th century Europe and the transcendent world, the purity, the order of heaven.
sentences.zh: 介于15世纪欧洲那个具体、物理的、充满暴力、残酷和危险的世界，与超越的、充满纯洁与天国秩序的世界之间。

sentences.en: They basically mediate between those two things, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们基本上在这两者之间起到了调解作用，不是吗？

sentences.en: And that's why, for someone like her, they have such cosmic...
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么对她这样的人来说，圣徒们具有如此宏大的……

sentences.en: Immediate presence.
sentences.zh: 即时显现的存在感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And significance.
sentences.zh: 以及非凡的意义。

sentences.en: They live in her heart as much as they do in her mind, presumably.
sentences.zh: 想必他们既活在她心中，也活在她脑海里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think that the closeness of the heavenly order, the supernatural order, is something that Joan, as she's growing up, completely takes for granted.
sentences.zh: 我认为，天国秩序、超自然秩序的切近感，是贞德在成长过程中完全视为理所当然的事。

sentences.en: Other people take it for granted too, but she is...
sentences.zh: 其他人也觉得理所当然，但她……

sentences.en: I mean, by the fact, the stuff about her kneeling when she hears the bells, she is peculiarly pious, do you think, even before her first supernatural visitations?
sentences.zh: 我是说，从她听到钟声就会下跪这件事来看，你认为她是否甚至在第一次经历超自然显灵之前就已经异常虔诚了？

sentences.en: Peculiarly pious, peculiarly impressionable, peculiarly imaginative, peculiarly self-confident as well, I think.
sentences.zh: 异常虔诚，异常易受感染，异常富有想象力，我想，也异常自信。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So I think a very distinctive little girl, probably.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得她可能是一个非常与众不同的小女孩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, you're not really selling her, to be honest, as a playmate, but actually, the people she's playing with are very different from the other puzzant children, right?
sentences.zh: 老实说，你这番描述并不觉得她是个适合一起玩耍的玩伴，但事实上，她一起玩耍的孩子们与其他底层农民儿童非常不同，对吧？

sentences.en: Because when she's 13 years old, actually, tellingly, when she's basically entering adolescence, I think, 1425, something happens.
sentences.zh: 因为当她13岁时——说来意味深长，当她基本上步入青春期时，大约在1425年，发生了一件事。

sentences.en: So tell us what happens.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲发生了什么吧。

sentences.en: Well, she described it herself in her trial.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她在审判中亲自描述过这件事。

sentences.en: The voice first came at noon on a summer's day in my father's garden, and she specified that this voice came from the direction of the village church,
sentences.zh: 声音是在一个夏日中午的父亲的花园里第一次出现的，她特意说明这个声音来自村里教堂的方向，

sentences.en: so that's where the bells would be rung from, and that it was bathed in light.
sentences.zh: 也就是钟声敲响的地方，并且声音沐浴在光芒之中。

sentences.en: And Joan insisted to inquisitors who were very skeptical about it, that right from the beginning, she had understood this voice to be good and worthy,
sentences.zh: 贞德向那些对此极其怀疑的审判官坚称，从一开始她就明白这个声音是善良且值得敬重的，

sentences.en: and that it was a voice sent from God to guide her.
sentences.zh: 它是上帝派来指引她的声音。

sentences.en: And she never let go of that assertion, and in time, she came to understand it as the voice, not of God himself, but of an angel, but she did not, to begin with, I think,
sentences.zh: 她从未动摇过这种说法，随着时间推移，她逐渐认识到这不是上帝本尊的声音，而是一位天使的声音，不过一开始，我想，

sentences.en: identify it with St. Michael specifically, nor with Catherine, nor with Margaret, although in the long run, she would.
sentences.zh: 她并没有将其具体认定为圣米迦勒，也没有认定为凯瑟琳或玛格丽特，尽管最终她会这么认为。

sentences.en: And to begin with, I don't think she had a sense, well, we will see, because the question of what these voices are, and what Joan thought the voices are,
sentences.zh: 而且一开始，我想她并没有明确的意识——嗯，我们拭目以待，因为关于这些声音到底是什么、贞德认为这些声音是什么的问题，

sentences.en: is a complex and fascinating one, and it will evolve, I think, over the course of her life.
sentences.zh: 是一个复杂而迷人的问题，我认为它会随着她的一生不断演变。

sentences.en: But what is absolutely clear is that she experiences it as real, and she essentially has conversations with this, initially it's a voice, then it becomes voice, multiple voices,
sentences.zh: 但绝对清楚的是，她对这些声音的体验是真实的，她基本上是在和这些声音对话——最初是一个声音，后来变成了多个声音，

sentences.en: but she has conversations with these voices in the way that she has conversations with everyone else, namely in a kind of very forthright, and kind of firm manner.
sentences.zh: 但她与这些声音对话的方式，就像她与其他人对话的方式一样，也就是一种非常直率、非常坚定的态度。

sentences.en: So if the voices tell her something that she doesn't agree with, she tells them that.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果声音告诉她一些她不同意的事情，她就会直言不讳地反驳它们。

sentences.en: Okay, that is unusual, because most people who hear voices, I mean, actually, madly,
sentences.zh: 好吧，这很不寻常，因为大多数听到幻听的人——说真的，疯狂的是，

sentences.en: the last person we talked about hearing voices was one of the suspects in the Jack the Ripper case.
sentences.zh: 我们上一个谈到听到幻听的人是开膛手杰克案的嫌疑人之一。

sentences.en: But when people hear voices, they then do what the voice tells them, they don't argue back with the voices.
sentences.zh: 但当人们听到幻听时，他们通常会照着声音的吩咐去做，而不会和幻听争辩。

sentences.en: And this is a contrast, as we'll come to, between Joan and other female mystics of the age, is that for Joan,
sentences.zh: 而接下来我们要谈到的一点是，贞德与这个时代其他女性神秘主义者的区别在于，对贞德来说，

sentences.en: these are kind of like voices that you might hear through headphones or something.
sentences.zh: 这些声音有点像你通过耳机或者其他什么东西听到的声音。

sentences.en: It's not entirely a mystic experience from her description of it.
sentences.zh: 从她对这段经历的描述来看，这并不完全是一次神秘的体验。

sentences.en: It's literally like you listening to Theo.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上，就像你在听西奥说话一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, quite like, well, yes, the messages that we get from Theo.
sentences.zh: 对，挺像的，呃，是的，就是我们从西奥那里收到的那些信息。

sentences.en: And these voices, to begin with, they offer her spiritual guidance, but then increasingly, they start to give her a political mission.
sentences.zh: 起初，这些声音为她提供精神上的指导，但随后，它们开始越来越多地赋予她一项政治使命。

sentences.en: And over the course of the months and then the years, this mission comes to be clarified.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，几个月又几年过去了，这项使命也变得清晰起来。

sentences.en: So to begin with, the voices are giving her a kind of vague instruction that she should go to the Dauphin and ride in front of him and drive the English out of France.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始，那些声音给她的指示有些模糊，说她应该去见王太子，骑马走在队伍前列，把英国人赶出法国。

sentences.en: Then it becomes more precise.
sentences.zh: 后来，指示变得更具体了。

sentences.en: She should lead the Dauphin to Reims and have him crowned there.
sentences.zh: 她应该带领王太子前往兰斯，并在那里为他加冕。

sentences.en: And then late in 1428, by which time the news of the siege at Orléans will have reached Dom Rémy, she's told by the voices to ride to Orléans and to break the English siege.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1428年底，奥尔良围城战的消息传到栋雷米时，神秘的声音告诉她，要骑马赶往奥尔良，打破英国人的包围。

sentences.en: And the voices, I mean, these are mad things to tell a teenage girl.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，对一个十几岁的女孩说这些简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But the voices say, well, don't worry, you know, we will guide you, we will support you throughout this mission that we've given you.
sentences.zh: 但那些声音说，别担心，你知道的，我们会引导你，在我们赋予你的整个使命中支持你。

sentences.en: And if you do as instructed, then in the long run, the whole of France will indeed be liberated from the English.
sentences.zh: 如果你照着指示去做，那么从长远来看，整个法国确实将从英国人手中解放出来。

sentences.en: And this liberation will be the ultimate proof in the eyes of the world that you are indeed on a mission from God.
sentences.zh: 在世人眼中，这种解放将成为最终的证明，证明你确实肩负着上帝的使命。

sentences.en: And you mentioned that Joan, you know, she answers back to the voices, but she never doubts their veracity, right?
sentences.zh: 你提到过，贞德会顶撞这些声音，但她从未怀疑过它们的真实性，对吧？

sentences.en: She never questions whether the voices might be demons or she might be misled because they're good.
sentences.zh: 她从不怀疑这些声音可能是恶魔，也不觉得自己会被误导，因为她觉得这些声音是好的。

sentences.en: She has a sense of them as good.
sentences.zh: 她感知到它们是善良的。

sentences.en: She has total confidence in what the voices are telling her.
sentences.zh: 她对这些声音告诉她的事情有着十足的信心。

sentences.en: And she actually, again, I think it's interesting that she's just, you know, entered her teens.
sentences.zh: 而且，我觉得有趣的是，她其实刚刚进入青春期，你知道的。

sentences.en: She takes a vow of chastity.
sentences.zh: 她发誓要保持贞洁。

sentences.en: So she's going to protect her virginity.
sentences.zh: 所以她要守护自己的童贞。

sentences.en: Her parents have lined up her fiancé for her.
sentences.zh: 她的父母已经为她物色好了一个未婚夫。

sentences.en: She says, you're out.
sentences.zh: 她说，没门。

sentences.en: I'm not interested in you.
sentences.zh: 我对你没兴趣。

sentences.en: And then we get to late 1428.
sentences.zh: 然后我们来到了1428年底。

sentences.en: So, you know, things are looking very dicey for the Dauphin, the French cause.
sentences.zh: 所以，局势对王太子和法国大业来说看起来非常棘手。

sentences.en: And this is the point when she decides, right, I'm going to do what the voice is telling me.
sentences.zh: 就在这个时候，她决定，对，我要按照这些声音告诉我的去做。

sentences.en: I'm going to get stuck in and begin the work of driving out the English.
sentences.zh: 我要卷入其中，开始把英国人赶出去的工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, but how do you begin?
sentences.zh: 对，但你该如何开始呢？

sentences.en: You're a peasant girl, you know, on the edge of things.
sentences.zh: 你只是个社会边缘的农家女孩，你知道的。

sentences.en: Where are you going to go?
sentences.zh: 你要去哪里？

sentences.en: There's only one place she really can go.
sentences.zh: 她其实只有一个地方可去。

sentences.en: And that is Vaucouleur, which is the one fortress in the region that is still holding out for the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 那就是沃库尔，那是该地区唯一一座仍在为王太子坚守的堡垒。

sentences.en: Under the command of Robert de Beaudricourt.
sentences.zh: 在罗贝尔·德·博德里库尔的指挥下。

sentences.en: And she tells her father, this is what I'm going to go and do.
sentences.zh: 她告诉父亲，这就是我要去做的事。

sentences.en: Her father is appalled.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲惊呆了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's already outraged that, you know, she's turned down the man that her father has chosen for her to marry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他已经很愤怒了，因为她拒绝了父亲为她挑选的结婚对象。

sentences.en: And also he's been having these nightmares in which he sees Joan running away with men at arMs.
sentences.zh: 而且他还一直在做噩梦，梦见贞德跟带兵的男人私奔了。

sentences.en: And the implication of that is that, you know, essentially he's worried that she is going to start misbehaving sexually.
sentences.zh: 这其中的潜台词就是，他基本上是在担心女儿会在私生活上出轨。

sentences.en: She's going to run away with a soldier.
sentences.zh: 她会和一个士兵私奔。

sentences.en: So she's now 16, what?
sentences.zh: 所以她现在16岁，多大来着？

sentences.en: She's about 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 她大约16岁。

sentences.en: I mean, any father, you know, your 16-year-old daughter comes to you and says, I'm basically going to run off and like join the army.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何父亲，当你的16岁女儿来找你说，我基本上要离家出走去参军了。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to go to a fortress full of men.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是要去一个到处都是男人的堡垒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, and come up, tell them some cock and bull story.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，编出一套荒诞不经的故事去告诉他们。

sentences.en: You'd be very, very worried.
sentences.zh: 你会非常非常担心。

sentences.en: You'd be perturbed.
sentences.zh: 你会感到焦虑不安。

sentences.en: So the thing is, Joan is a runaway.
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，贞德是个离家出走的人。

sentences.en: You know, she deliberately ignores her father's orders and runs away to Vaucouleur full of violent soldiers and men.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她故意无视父亲的命令，逃到了充满暴力士兵和男人的沃库尔。

sentences.en: And she goes to Vaucouleur, who's, he's a quite unscrupulous person, we've already said.
sentences.zh: 她去找了沃库尔，正如我们之前所说，这是一个相当不择手段的人。

sentences.en: So kind of quite a dangerous man.
sentences.zh: 所以算是一个相当危险的男人。

sentences.en: She goes to him and she explains her mission.
sentences.zh: 她去找他，并解释了自己的使命。

sentences.en: And he, first time he says, you're mad, go away.
sentences.zh: 第一次，他说，你疯了，走开。

sentences.en: Second time, you're mad, go away.
sentences.zh: 第二次，你疯了，走开。

sentences.en: She's still hanging around in Vaucouleur.
sentences.zh: 她依然在沃库尔盘桓。

sentences.en: She's ignoring what Vaucouleur has said.
sentences.zh: 她完全不理会沃库尔的话。

sentences.en: So in January 1429, Vaucouleur comes to the house in Vaucouleur where Joan has been staying.
sentences.zh: 所以在1429年1月，沃库尔来到了贞德一直借住的沃库尔宅邸。

sentences.en: And he has brought the local priest with him.
sentences.zh: 并且他还带来了当地的神父。

sentences.en: And he tells the priest, this girl is possessed by an evil spirit.
sentences.zh: 他告诉神父，这个女孩被邪灵附体了。

sentences.en: Exorcise the evil spirit.
sentences.zh: 驱逐这个邪灵。

sentences.en: But Joan just kneels in front of the priest and reproaches the priest and says, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 但贞德只是在神父面前跪下，责备神父并说道，你在做什么？

sentences.en: You've heard my confession.
sentences.zh: 你听过我的告解。

sentences.en: You know that I am literally on the side of the angels.
sentences.zh: 你知道我确确实实是站在天使这一边的。

sentences.en: And so the priest says, well, you know, she's not possessed.
sentences.zh: 于是神父说，好吧，你知道的，她没有被附身。

sentences.en: There's nothing I can do here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里什么也做不了。

sentences.en: And so Joan stands up and she turns to Vaucouleur.
sentences.zh: 于是贞德站起身，转向沃库尔。

sentences.en: And a third time she says, take me to the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 第三次，她说，带我去见王太子。

sentences.en: And this time, the Vaucouleur relents.
sentences.zh: 这一次，沃库尔心软了。

sentences.en: And this might be on his own initiative, or it might be that he has received word from his two regional overlords.
sentences.zh: 这可能是他自己的主意，也可能是他收到了他那两个地区高级领主的信件。

sentences.en: And these are a guy called Charles, the Duke of Lorraine, and René of Anjou.
sentences.zh: 这两个人一个叫夏尔，是洛林公爵，另一个是安茹的勒内。

sentences.en: And René of Anjou is the second son of Yolande, the mother-in-law of the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 而安茹的勒内是王太子岳母约兰德的第二个儿子。

sentences.en: So why do these two guys, who are serious people, you know, aristocratic people, power brokers, why on earth would they be encouraging what clearly de Baudricourt himself,
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么这两个严肃的人，你知道的，贵族人物、政治掮客，为什么他们会去鼓励这样一个连德·博德里库尔自己——

sentences.en: another serious person, thinks is a sort of loony girl who's just got mad crackpot ideas?
sentences.zh: 另一个严肃的人——都认为是个满口荒诞疯话的怪异女孩的想法呢？

sentences.en: Why do they indulge this?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要去纵容这种事？

sentences.en: Well, Charles of Lorraine is very ill at the time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，当时的洛林公爵病得很重。

sentences.en: And he's been brought word that there's this girl claiming a mission from God.
sentences.zh: 并且有人向他报告说，有个女孩声称自己肩负着上帝的使命。

sentences.en: And this isn't massively unusual.
sentences.zh: 这并不是非常罕见的事情。

sentences.en: You know, every so often, it's usually girls, but sometimes boys as well, will appear claiming that they've got messages from God.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每隔一段时间，通常是女孩，但有时也有男孩，会出现并声称他们得到了来自上帝的信息。

sentences.en: And they are often capable of performing incredible miracles.
sentences.zh: 而且他们往往能够创造出不可思议的奇迹。

sentences.en: And so I think that Charles of Lorraine hopes that perhaps Joan will heal him.
sentences.zh: 所以我想洛林公爵是希望贞德或许能治好他的病。

sentences.en: But Joan says, no, I'm not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 但贞德说，不，我不会这么做。

sentences.en: I, you know, I can't heal anyone.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，我谁也治不了。

sentences.en: And in this, again, she's unusual.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，她也是与众不同的。

sentences.en: The only thing she does miraculous is her mission.
sentences.zh: 她所做的唯一奇迹就是她的使命。

sentences.en: You know, she's not going around healing the sick or, you know, anything like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她并没有到处去医治病人或做诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: And she dismisses it as nonsense.
sentences.zh: 她把这斥为无稽之谈。

sentences.en: Why would I be able to heal anyone?
sentences.zh: 我怎么可能会治好任何人？

sentences.en: That's not what I can do.
sentences.zh: 那不是我能做的事。

sentences.en: And Charles is not offended by this.
sentences.zh: 而夏尔对此并不生气。

sentences.en: In fact, he's rather impressed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他印象相当深刻。

sentences.en: And he gives her some money and he gives her a horse.
sentences.zh: 他给了她一些钱，还送了她一匹马。

sentences.en: Because, of course, she's going to need a horse if she's going to ride all the way to the Dauphin, who's in Chalons, just south of the Loire, which is about 300 miles away.
sentences.zh: 因为当然了，如果她要一路骑马去见位于卢瓦尔河以南不远的沙隆的王太子——大约有300英里远——她肯定需要一匹马。

sentences.en: As for René of Anjou, you know, we've said he's the brother of the Dauphin's queen.
sentences.zh: 至于安茹的勒内，正如我们所说，他是王太子王后的兄弟。

sentences.en: He really has a stake in ensuring that the Dauphin stays in the fight.
sentences.zh: 他确实有切身利害关系去确保王太子能继续战斗下去。

sentences.en: And he may well think, as Yolande may well have thought, well, you know, I mean, let's try.
sentences.zh: 他很可能会想，正如约兰德可能也想过的那样，好吧，你知道的，我们不妨试一试。

sentences.en: What have we got to lose?
sentences.zh: 我们有什么好失去的？

sentences.en: I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: And there's probably also a slight element of like, come on, let's just get rid of her.
sentences.zh: 而且可能也夹杂着一点这种情绪：得了吧，干脆把她打发走得了。

sentences.en: Tell her to go.
sentences.zh: 叫她走人。

sentences.en: No, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: You don't think so?
sentences.zh: 你觉得不是吗？

sentences.en: You think they believe in it?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他们相信这事？

sentences.en: I think they actively think we've got nothing to lose.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们实际上觉得我们横竖没有什么可失去的。

sentences.en: She may be what she says she is.
sentences.zh: 她可能真的是她所说的那种人。

sentences.en: I think they are very, very interested in what Joan has to say, because I think they're desperate.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们对贞德要说的话非常非常感兴趣，因为我觉得他们已经绝望了。

sentences.en: De Bodricor definitely still has reservations, because what happens now is a very controversial development in Joan's story.
sentences.zh: 德·博德里库尔显然仍有保留，因为接下来发生的是贞德故事中一个极具争议的发展。

sentences.en: Joan says, OK, I'm going on this mission.
sentences.zh: 贞德说，好吧，我要去执行这个使命了。

sentences.en: I need male clothing if I'm going to go.
sentences.zh: 如果我要去的话，我需要男装。

sentences.en: And de Bodricor gives her male clothing.
sentences.zh: 于是德·博德里库尔给了她男装。

sentences.en: But we know from later source, which describes his reaction to it, that he handed this male clothing over only with the utmost repugnance, to quote the court records.
sentences.zh: 但从后来描述他对此反应的史料中我们得知，正如法庭记录所引用的那样，他交出这些男装时内心充满了极度的厌恶。

sentences.en: And this isn't surprising because the 15th century, it's fair to say, is not a trans-friendly era.
sentences.zh: 这并不奇怪，因为15世纪可以说是绝对不赞成跨性别者的时代。

sentences.en: So cross-dressing is seen as being an abomination unto God.
sentences.zh: 所以女扮男装被视为对上帝的亵渎。

sentences.en: So we've said that Joan is very pious, but when she wants to, she's perfectly capable of ignoring a direct biblical dictate.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说过贞德非常虔诚，但当她愿意的时候，她完全有能力无视《圣经》的直接训诫。

sentences.en: So I don't want to plunge into my sceptical amateur psychology too much straight away.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想马上就陷入我那怀疑论者的业余心理学分析中。

sentences.en: But to say she's entered her teens, she's taken a vow of chastity, protecting her virginity is incredibly important to her.
sentences.zh: 但要说的是，她刚进入青春期，发誓要保持贞洁，守护童贞对她来说极其重要。

sentences.en: And she now says she wants to dress as a man.
sentences.zh: 而现在她说她想穿男装。

sentences.en: Then there are, you know, implications for this.
sentences.zh: 这里面自然就有了种种暗示。

sentences.en: Maybe let's say secular, secular minded listeners might draw implications from this about what is actually nagging at her.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以说，思想世俗的听众可能会从中推断出究竟是什么在一直困扰着她。

sentences.en: We should wait until we've told her whole story and listen to what she actually has to say at the trial before kind of trying to work out what might have been going on here.
sentences.zh: 在我们试图弄清楚这里可能发生了什么之前，我们应该等到讲完她的整个故事，并听听她在审判时究竟说了些什么。

sentences.en: But I hear you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 但我懂你的意思，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I hear you.
sentences.zh: 我懂你的意思。

sentences.en: Anyway, so she has her outfit of male clothes.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，总之她换上了男装。

sentences.en: She has her hair cropped into the kind of, you know, the nightly pudding bowl that anyone who's seen the painting of Henry V will recognise.
sentences.zh: 她的头发被剪成了那种骑士式的布丁碗发型，任何看过亨利五世画像的人都会认得出来。

sentences.en: She's got her horse.
sentences.zh: 她有了马。

sentences.en: She's been given a sword, which anyone with nightly pretensions needs.
sentences.zh: 她得到了一把剑，这是任何有骑士野心的人所必需的。

sentences.en: And de Beaudricourt has given her two pages and, intriguingly, four men at arMs.
sentences.zh: 而且德·博德里库尔给她派了两名侍童，更有趣的是，还派了四名武装士兵。

sentences.en: So her father's dream has come true.
sentences.zh: 所以她父亲的噩梦成真了。

sentences.en: Oh no, her father must be gutted.
sentences.zh: 哦不，她父亲一定心碎欲绝。

sentences.en: And of course they are there to guard her because they are going to be riding across what is effectively bandit territory.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们呆在那里是为了保护她，因为他们将穿过实际上是土匪横行的地盘。

sentences.en: And this also is, you know, you could say, well,
sentences.zh: 这也是，你可以说，

sentences.en: it's a sensible precaution for any girl who is going to ride 300 odd miles through a war zone to disguise the fact that she is female.
sentences.zh: 对于任何一个要骑马穿越战区300多英里的女孩来说，伪装自己的女性身份是一个明智的防范措施。

sentences.en: Although it has to be said that at no point does Joan ever justify her cross-dressing in those terMs.
sentences.zh: 尽管必须指出的是，贞德从未在这些层面上为她的女扮男装辩护过。

sentences.en: And the clear implication, which in time she will make explicit, is that her voice has told her to dress in male clothes.
sentences.zh: 而显而易见的暗示（她日后会将其明确表述出来）是，她的声音告诉她要穿男装。

sentences.en: That it's not a question of practicality and pragmatism.
sentences.zh: 这并非出于实用性或务实主义的考量。

sentences.en: She never says that.
sentences.zh: 她从未这么说过。

sentences.en: She never says that.
sentences.zh: 她从未说过。

sentences.en: And the male clothing, as we will see in our next episode, serves for her, well, we will tease out what it means to her, but it is clearly something very, very spiritually,
sentences.zh: 正如我们将在下一集里看到的那样，男装对她而言——好吧，我们会剖析它对她意味着什么，但它显然在精神上、

sentences.en: psychologically, symbolically significant to her.
sentences.zh: 心理上和象征意义上对她非常非常重要。

sentences.en: But why, what does it have to do with her mission?
sentences.zh: 但为什么呢，这和她的使命有什么关系？

sentences.en: What are her voices?
sentences.zh: 她的那些声音到底是什么？

sentences.en: These are all questions that we will explore perhaps,
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们将要探讨的问题，也许吧，

sentences.en: or we'll start exploring in our next episode when Joan arrives at the court of the Dauphin and reveals to the Dauphin the mission that she has been given by God.
sentences.zh: 或者我们将在下一集开始探讨，当时贞德抵达了王太子的宫廷，并向王太子展示了上帝赋予她的使命。

sentences.en: And very exciting, and actually I have to say, an absolutely fascinating story.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋，而且我必须说，这是一个绝对引人入胜的故事。

sentences.en: I remember when you were researching this, Tom, you were saying to me, this is one of the most intriguing stories we've done on the Restus History,
sentences.zh: 我记得你在做这方面的研究时，汤姆，你曾对我说，这是我们在《余烬历史》中做过的最吸引人的故事之一，

sentences.en: and it's certainly panning out that way.
sentences.zh: 而且事实也确实如此发展着。

sentences.en: So, if you want to find out what happens when Joan arrives at the Dauphin's court, whether she succeeds in saving Orléans from the English,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想知道当贞德到达王太子宫廷时发生了什么，她是否成功地将奥尔良从英国人手中解救出来，

sentences.en: we're going to be telling the whole story in the next three episodes.
sentences.zh: 我们将在接下来的三集里讲述整个故事。

sentences.en: And if you're a member of the Restus History Club, you can hear those episodes straight away.
sentences.zh: 如果你是雷斯图斯历史俱乐部的会员，你可以立即收听这些单集。

sentences.en: If you would like to start the new year on an inspiring and exciting note,
sentences.zh: 如果你想以一个充满启发和激动人心的方式开始新的一年，

sentences.en: then do join the Restus History Club at therestushistory.com because we are planning all kinds of exciting benefits for you this year.
sentences.zh: 那就请登录 therestushistory.com 加入雷斯图斯历史俱乐部吧，因为我们今年正为你筹划各种令人兴奋的福利。

sentences.en: Not just the usual ad-free listening and early access to series, but all sorts of thrilling bonus series to come for club members only.
sentences.zh: 不仅有常规的无广告收听和提前收听节目的权限，还有各种仅限俱乐部会员专享的精彩番外系列。

sentences.en: However, the key thing is Joan of Arc and what will happen next in her story, and that is what we will be investigating next time.
sentences.zh: 然而，关键在于圣女贞德以及她故事的下一步发展，这正是我们下次要探讨的内容。

sentences.en: Au revoir.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Au revoir.
sentences.zh: 再见。
